Hey Mark! Im the developer of the first two games, and Im beyond happy that you played them and genuinely grateful for the kind words you said about my games. It means the world to me and gives me so much motivation to keep building this universe and keep making games in general.

I've been watching you for a long time, and it s always been a dream of mine for you to notice my work. Seeing this video is honestly one of the best things that's happened to me in a while.

Ill admit, its a little bittersweet that you found my games now, because Im not fully confident in them yet  I can see a lot of flaws and I'm constantly trying to improve. But thank you so much for playing them and for appreciating the atmosphere I was going for! The reason theyre on the shorter side is because my old computer broke down, and lately Ive been working on much weaker hardware, which makes development really tough. But I keep pushing forward because I want to create something bigger something that really resonates with people. And it means so much that you enjoyed whats there already, even though I didnt think it was good enough to get this kind of attention.

Once again, thank you so much for the video and for the kind words!

P.S. I saw a lot of people in the comments joking (or maybe being serious, I honestly can't tell) about a movie or something like that. I have no idea how realistic that is, but if you ever want to do something like that or collaborate in any way, feel free to reach out to me via email! I'd be absolutely thrilled!

Distractable single handedly is the one thing that kept me going when I had to work a job I absolutely hated. I worked full time, 40 hours a week at pick n save. 3rd shift stock position. I couldn't leave due to a shitty situation where I was being financially abused by my ex. They roped me into paying all of the bills by getting me signed on to things with them like car insurance, registration, rent, etc. Then they quit their job so I was at risk of being held accountable legally as well if things werent paid. My mental health was at it's absolute lowest. I was scared of my own thoughts and would cry in the bathroom on the clock because of how awful it was. My entire crew had quit, and I was left doing a job meant for a team of at LEAST 5. Pulling in 5 truck loads a night of 7+ pallets each, putting the entire load from the night before out on the shelves, answering phone calls, cleaning the whole store, and facing it too among other things. This podcast was the only thing that made it all even a little bearable. It made me actually laugh out loud and made time go by so much faster. It gave my mind a place to escape to instead of wandering somewhere dark. It gave me hope. Now, I'm free of that relationship, have been cut loose of all financial responsibilities associated to them, and am finality going back to school to get my associates degree like I had been wanting to the whole time. My mentality has never been more positive and I have never been so excited to see where life leads me. I absolutely love to be in class and to learn and have found out more about myself now than I ever had before everything. Thank you guys for everything you do. I'm so glad I found y'all

I really love this game. Here‘s what I‘ve been able to deduce for some folks who might wanna discuss story beats:

The game is intentionally vague about whether or not Whiskers is a supernatural entity (demon, devil, etc.) or a biological predator hunting off instinct. It used both heavy religious symbolism in the documents, mainly from the way cultures who previously encountered it dealt with the creature while also showing the research and biological concepts applied by the grandpa and his university team. The notions you teach it during the language teaching parts seem to be obvious symbolisms tying into the games plot „meaning, language“ etc. all relate to the theme of theory of mind and how the entity seems to both understand the world around it through implicit mimicry, but one could not  be sure whether or not it was just an instinctual automaton that merely mirrors instead of understanding. It also asks the question of what one means by „understand“. I really love the tie ins with the neuroscience bits by the gamedev, particularly regarding shamans who have facial blindness being required to deal with the creature because it cannot feed off of their representations of other people for further cycles. These themes seem to also be underscored by the split between its shell and inner core. The core appears to be quasi static and somewhat conscious retaining some information about previous cycles throughout its regenerations, as it mentions memories of being buried (possibly by shamans) in a graveyard sometime in the stone age (it is confused by all our modern concepts and complications of mind), while the shell seems to be more dynamic but also animalistic and in control (the core grandpa when being released speaks of „being used“ by the outer shell and that he cannot resist against its urges). The core might also simply be used by the shell as an anglerfish would use its antenna, as a lure so it might not be conscious at all (which the scientists constantly doubt). This is all just scratching the surface of a game that has fantastic visuals, atmosphere and eery gameplay. A true marvel of a horror game!

I noticed there's actually a strategy with not immediately outing the ghost.

If you narrowed it down to a particular animatronic, you can repair the rest of them before expelling the ghost. Then right as soon as you do so, call the previously possessed animatronic in for repairs; it prevents them from being possessed twice in a row and keeps stability up for everyone.

That's why BB's gimmick is the way it is. It makes it extremely obvious that hey, yeah, BB's possessed, but you can't read BB's condition, so you can't employ this strategy while BB is possessed, or risk failure.

This fan game is a nice addition to everything else existing into the timeline, and patches up some rougher areas of the timeline, whether intended or not…

14:32 Interestingly enough, what Mattpat is talking about here is actually being talked about in the writing community right now. It's becoming more popular for people to release a bunch of short, tropey books iback to back the same way one would do with fanfiction than it is for people to work on longer, deeper works. Absolutely find to do with fanfiction, it's supposed to be just for fun, and tropes are not a bad thing, so long as the story, characters, etc. have more to them than said trope. But, if you just focus a book on one trope...yeah, probably not going to be very deep. Which is also fine, the issue isn't in the writers but the industry favoring this and pressuring a lot of writers to do it this way if you want to be popular or traditionally published. So, sad to hear it is happening with a lot of different media too. I'd say it mostly has to do with the industry involved with the creations of this media rather than the creators themselves, and the fact the pressure is being put on the creators who should have much more freedom is sad.

This was such a good representation of the original backrooms concept. It's empty. There's nothing. No stupid monsters. You wander and wander under the humming flourescent lights and you think there _must_ be *_something_* here. You're so desperate for anything to break up the monotony of endless wandering and the incessant hum of the lights that you trick yourself into seeing and hearing things. It happened constantly to Mark throughout this video, and it's proof of concept that the backrooms never needed monsters.

Edit 2: I'd like to amend a few things. Firstly, yes the original greentext does say something along the lines of "god forbid you hear something because if you heard it, it certainly heard you." This is not explicit confirmation of a monster inside the backrooms, it is an implication at best. Remember that the backrooms are based on "liminal" spaces, at least according to how the aesthetic has changed the meaning of that word. These images are of public spaces that should be teeming with people, but are empty and usually taken with dim lighting to give them an abandoned or dilapidated appearance. They're supposed to invoke unease and loneliness. This game achieves that same feeling by not having anything truly threaten you. Second, I had not seen kane's videos before this, and I do like his monster, but you'll notice he spends a lot of time building up to them and they aren't the only source of horror. There are the disappearances and strange events, anything could happen in kane's backrooms! Lastly, yes, there are a couple instances of an appendage of some kind disappearing behind a pillar in the video. But still, nothing happens. To me, it seems to be presented as your mind playing tricks on you, as I said above. I don't think every horror experience needs to be an adrenaline pumping sprint away from a screaming monstrosity that wants you dead. Sometimes isolation and hopelessness are all you need, and that's what I was trying to praise in this comment. Thanks to everyone for their likes and replies, whether you agreed with me or not!

What I’ve learned from the comments:

1. This is what the back rooms were meant to be. Pure nothingness. No silly monsters. Just you and your increasing level of insanity.

2. The mind plays tricks on itself. When it’s bored, it makes things up.

3. It’s the fear of nothing that’s more scary than the fear of something. It makes you uneasy and longing for something, anything.

4. The point of the back rooms is displacement. Feeling like you’re the only thing in a supposedly man-made place, but also feeling as if you’re not supposed to be there. Like nothing in there should be living, yet there you are. 

5. Our brains will betray us more than help us. It will fill in the voids and come up with theories other than the truth. 

6. Mark gave the perfect reaction and is quite simply entertaining in stressful, seemingly boring scenarios. We love you, Mark!

That last ending was beautiful and the trophy name is so fitting: "Closure".

Closure means fully accepting and letting go of what once was, and creating new possibilities, relationships, rituals, and goals moving forward.

The developer even got the scene right because that's what a therapist would try to help you with. To visualize the person you need to have closure with and imagine what they would tell you if they were infront of you. They (the person you lost and love) don't want you to be suffering, hurting yourself or being stuck in a never ending cycle depression, they want you to move on with your life and be happy but that's the hard part because sometimes we feel we disrespect their memory by moving on with our lives without them.

However that's the beauty of this scene, since it portrays how that closure should look like with that person that we love and loved us, it's sincere, honest, without guilt, with their hearts and words full of love and kindness. 

That is closure and i hope, if someone reads this and is suffering like this, you get the closure you deserve.

Them talking about Unus Annus ending hit me in the feels real hard, and here's why:

My ex Fiance and I were planning our wedding around the time Unus Annus started. we were fans of Mark and I watched Ethans videos on occasion, so a collaborative project with both of them was amazing!
Around February-March of 2020, my fiance and I had a horrible break-up that still haunts me to this day on occasion. We were so incredibly close to being married. She moved out of the house and took the dog with her. The house fell silent, save for the laughter of Mark and Ethan.

Death is inevitable, and all things good and bad have to come to an end at some point. Unus Annus helped me learn this lesson before I was able to spiral out of control and bring my timer to zero myself before life did.
And when the timer reached zero at 3AM EST, I was there when the screen went black. When I saw my reflection in my screen, I learned that even though it is over, I can celebrate what was good and still be happy even when things seem bleak.
I have a tattoo now, 00:00:00:01. A constant reminder that as long as I have the will to move forward, and air in my lungs, I will never let my timer reach zero.

Mark and Ethan, if you ever see this,  know that you were there for me when nothing else was. Unus Annus was there for me during some of the best and worst times of my life. Unus Annus saw my triumphs, reveled in my accomplishments, and supported me during my time of need. Unus Annus witnessed my world shattering all around me, and was there to help me pick up the pieces to begin rebuilding it. Unus Annus saw me through my personal path to recovery as I was navigating life without my co-pilot. 

Words cannot begin to describe how thankful I am for both of you and Unus Annus. So from the bottom of my heart..

Notes for future horror game developers: 
- If you put a knocking sound in only one direction, there's a pretty good chance that your players do not have a door on that side of their room. Put it on *both* channels, not just right or left.
- Random images and weird text are not scary.
- If I'm listening to a 911 call, and the _caller_ is as disaffected as the callers are here, the caller *is* the dangerous entity.
- It is not illegal to keep to your home, even if you are witnessing a crime in progress. Obvious lack of research is obvious.
- When creating a monster, "looks like humans with a slight disfigurement" is not that scary. Go big or go home.

This game really reminds me of the story “The Tell-Tale Heart” by Edgar Allen Poe. For some people that don’t know the story: A man was living with an elderly man who had, he called it, one “filmy pale-blue vulture-eye” which he hated. He loved the old man dearly and had no reason to do him harm, yet one day he had plotted to murder the old man because of the eye. For seven nights the man would constantly peek in the old man’s room, giving just enough light to shine onto the old man’s eye. On the eighth night the old man woke up as the narrator slips up and makes a noise, the narrator lights a lantern and shines it right in the vulture-eye. The old man’s heart began to beat very loudly, louder and louder, so the man decided to strike. He made careful calculation of the murder, attempting the perfect crime, complete with dismembering the body in the bathtub and hiding it under the floorboards. Yet right when he hid the body parts he kept hearing a thumping sound which he thought was the dead man’s heart. The next day the police arrived asking if everything was ok, and the man invited them in thinking there was no way they would find the old man. The thumping grew increasingly loud, and he thought the police could hear it (they couldn’t). So he confessed and dug up the floorboards to reveal the old man. As it turned out, there was no actual heartbeat, it was the man’s guilt of killing him, and the guilt was constantly hearing the heartbeat (the final thing that he heard from the old man) remembering what he had done.

This game seems to be partially inspired by the story of The Tell-Tale Heart. An Edgar Allen Poe story about a man who lives with an old dude with a creepy eye. The man becomes increasingly convinced the old man’s eye is evil, so much so the man kills the old man. And when the police come to investigate the sounds he confesses to the crime solely because he believes the cops can hear the man’s heart beating under the floorboards like he can. Though the man thinks it’s the old man’s heart beating, many interpret that it’s the own man’s heart beating

As much as I do miss the "old Markiplier and Jacksepticeye", content like this where the two are just having a mature talk about their audience, life, job, struggles, morals and opinions could've never come from the hyper Sean and Mark from the previous decade. I've been watching both of you for close to that (probably started around 2015), and I can say that they have both grown exponentially. A lot of what they've said here is very relatable and cool to see. I still look for the channels that can connect with their viewers on more than an acquaintance or monetary level. As much as you both state you don't hold that connection, you really do, just as any celebrity you have influence over lives. No better example than MatPat's recent retirement, the internet was in shock, people literally mourned his retirement like he died, simply because he made a difference in so many hearts. Regardless of how disconnected you can feel from your fans, the words and actions you say and perform can affect them mentally, which by proxy can affect them physically. Like you even stated with TikTok not being capable of this relationship between creator and audience, that is very true and it goes for every one of these "short form social media" sites, except maybe Vine (RIP). TikTok, Snapchat, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts all have the same issue, the content isn't enticing enough to make a watcher explore the channels.
Most the videos I see on YouTube Shorts are enticing, I like the content and the creators are interesting, and maybe they appear in my recommendations a handful of times afterwards, but I heard this line and I don't remember where but it's a great question: can you remember a single creator's name that you've viewed on a short form social media site? The person I heard this from had asked others, most the people they asked couldn't name a single one. I know so many creators I've seen multiple times on YouTube Shorts, and I don't even remember their channel's initials. The bond between audience and creator is non-existent. Another good example is viewing their long-form videos compared to their Shorts. The long-form videos from these mainly Shorts creators always have VERY low view counts, even when the channel has millions of subscribers the long-form videos are usually between 5k-50k views which is awful for a channel that successful. There isn't a motivation to look into a creator, short form content just can't do it. Vine was really the only one I'd say that could, since many of those creators were memorable, and made successful jumps to other platforms, like Thomas Sanders or Zach King.

This is related to how YouTube handles urls. Anything after "watch" or "shorts" is handled as a url for a video or short. However, when you remove any letter from these two words. YouTube then tries to load the channel profile that has set up watc as its url redirect. The channel 666 happens to have it's redirect url as watc. There's also another channel that pops up if you leave only "ah" in it. That one is perfectly normal and has a name corresponding to these two letters.

Mark, there are other combinations: “tc”, “tch”, “atc” and “at”.

They all lead to other channels.

so someone on the og video confirmed that the reason you can do this with any video is because
" it's making use of 2 channels, 1 with the username of 666 and another with the username of watc. when you remove 'h' from the url of a random video, it can't phrase the query string (the part after the '?') anymore, as it's a query string for the watch url. So instead, it tries to open the profile with the name watc. youtube channel settings allows you to set a redirect url for a specific channel, so what this user has done is have the channel of watc redirect to the video uploaded by user 666. "

We did touch-typing when I was in school, and I loathed it with a fiery passion. I look at the keyboard when I type, had to for years because those lessons did not help me learn. What finally did help me? Playing keyboard-dependent video games on my PC.
I mostly play in the dark, and after a while I just learned from rote where all the keys are in relation to each other. Probably my biggest hurdle (and subsequently my best teacher) was ARK: Survival Evolved. Sooooo many keybindings to remember in that game!
Between that and modded Minecraft, I no longer have to do my old hunt-and-peck style unless I'm typing something long-winded like these comments on Youtube. The only real problem I have these days is switching from real keyboards to the one on my phone and the one on my ipad, because they all have slightly different layouts for the punctuation and I find that really irritating, but it's not the end of the world.

Also, that program not allowing you to use backspace is stupid. They should have two modes, compare your speed and accuracy when allowed to use it with your speed and accuracy when not allowed. I think their concern is that a sloppy typist will be slower, but you can get pretty fast at correcting your mistakes on the fly if you're aware you hit the wrong key (which I pretty much always am, and from Mark's frustrated noises, he was, too).
The assumption, in my eyes, is that you're hitting the wrong keys from inexperience...I've been typing since I was 5, so that's not my problem. I hit the wrong keys because my hands twitch. They always have, they always will. I've learned to work around it.

So, I went to a parkour gym once and my experience was somewhat similar to Mark's. Well, without the cops bit. This was an actual gym with padded floors and proper climbing equipment to practice on safely. Not the sink-or-swim approach of falling off the side of a parking garage. 

It was front flip day. The set up was a 15-ish foot stretch of mats, then a short barrier (probably 1.5 - 2 feet tall) and then a set mats behind it to land on. Similar to Mark, I'd also made a... calculated error. I'd never done a proper front flip before; Only ever into a swimming pool. Otherwise, I had no parkour experience, whatsoever. I'd seen people do flips, watched some videos on how to do flips, and understood the basics of how to do a flip successfully. So I'd thought.

And so, we were all lined up taking turns flipping over this obstacle. Everyone's doing fine. Perfect front flip after perfect front flip.  Then, it was my turn to go. I take a second to kind of figure out my approach. Figure out what foot I'm going to start on, how I'm going to launch into this thing, and then I just go for it.  As I'm running up to the barricade, all I'm thinking is, "Okay, I just need to get my ass over my head. Once I'm there, reflexes will take over."

I cleared the barrier, ass over head, exactly as planned. I started bringing the feet around, so far so good. Then, I landed FLAT on my ass. To my surprise, it didn't hurt quite like a bitch. It hurt like 5 bitches. It felt like I'd been fist-fucked by Edward Scissorhands. It felt like I was now 3 inches shorter than before I made questionable life choices. 

A couple onlookers heard my "OW, FUCK!" distress call and promptly dragged my assless remains back to the starting area. I didn't break anything, thankfully. It only hurt for a few days, and I was fine. However, I realized right then and there that maybe parkour is not my thing. I like being able to walk comfortably and unassisted. I haven't been back since, nor have I attempted any parkour-related stunts since then. And I have no intention to.

The goal of the roll is to disperse as much of the impact across your body as possible, so it's not all concentrated in one spot and busting bones.

If you find yourself in this situation (2nd story, 0 rolling capacity) then the 2nd most useful thing would be a break-fall. But let's say you've never done that either and need the babiest easiest thing possible that *might* still leave you with some bones.

Okay here's the plan: Land on your feet and lean forward, but keep yours knees nice and loose, your goal is to immediately let your legs collapse so you can fall forward.

You know the gesture you make when you want to pretend to be cat? (hand by your head, palm facing out, so you can go "meow meow!") That's right, we're gonna make like a cat (who always lands on his feet) and nyan-nyan as we fall. (Keep your palms flat though or you may break a knuckle). Fall forward, and let your nyan-arms help cushion the impact so you don't bust a rib.

Finally most important: Turn your head to your side before it impacts the ground or you WILL bust a nose. So make like a Jesus-cat and turn the other cheek.

TLDR! Be the nyan-cat: land *lightly* on your feet, surrender the knees, nyan with your arms, fall forward, face cheek to ground.

This game is actually based off of the Japanese urban legend Aka Manto, and the tall person in the red cloak is meant to Aka Manto.  He basically haunts bathrooms and will ask you for blue or red paper.  There are a lot of variations, but choosing blue can get you strangled and choosing red can get you stabbed.  If you ask for a different paper, he drags you into the underworld.  The only ways to escape are by ignoring him, running away, or saying you don't want paper.

Tips and trivia for _Aka Manto_ :

_Aka Manto_ , literally "red cape" (originally "red jacket) is a figure from Japanese urban legend.  If you are using a public toilet, _Aka Manto_ may come to you and ask if you would prefer red paper or blue paper.  Choose red, and you receive a bloody death.  Choose blue and you receive a death that removes all of your blood or suffocates you.  Choose another color and _Aka Manto_ gets... creative.  The only safe response is not to answer, or to state that you have no preference, and/or to run away as fast as you can.

_Ofuda_ :  This is a slip of blessed paper, imbued with the power of the local temple's deity.  This one looks to be a _shinsatsu_ , meaning it needs to be placed at the local shrine's altar.  In this game, the shrine also has a sword, which can be used against _Aka Manto_ .  But you need all the colored papers to get it.  Speaking of which, the Well has the Blue Paper, so you'll need to find that coin.

The Anatomy Model holds the key to escaping the school.  The pieces are the Nose, the Ribcage (both of which you found), the Eyes (near the Pool), the Brain (exit the girl's bathroom and go R-L-R), the Left Arm (from the last room, go L-L-R), the Right Arm (in the Library) and the Organ (also in the Library, but you need to find the three red books to get it).

The other two requirements to escaping the school are a koppe pan (roll from the lunch room) and some milk.  You'll see why when you get to the roof.

Aka Manto: A Japanese urban legend of a spirit that appears in bathrooms. It will ask the occupant if they want red or blue paper; both choices ending in a grim fate. If you choose red paper, the Aka Monto will tear you limb from limb, staining the stalls red with blood. If you choose blue, then Aka Monto will strangle you until your blue in the face. The only way to avoid the spirit is to choose neither paper, ignore it, or confuse the spirit with a third optional colored paper.

The game is difficult, it's designed to have you running around with items (small inventory and lots of items that are used on the other side of the map). 
There are 7 pieces of paper and 7 anatomy items; either set leads to an ending, but finding the full set is difficult enough for someone who doesn't know the map.

Aka Manto does love spawning near you as well, making the achievement for completing it without getting hit once very fun.

Gotta say, this game reminds me of "The Nun Massacre" that Mark played a few years back; y'all can find it on "3 Scary Games #11". It literally has the same formula with how the game works; referring to the windy interior of the building layout (you can also crawl in the vents), having to find various items (including anatomy parts) and notes, and having a (possessed?) nun with a knife chasing you. The only difference between "Aka Manto" and "The Nun Massacre" is the story, its characters, and the setting ("A.M." being set at an abandoned haunted school and "T.N.M." at a boarding school on top of a mountain). 
What I like about these two games are their atmosphere, the sense of being lost, and the sounds. Both the antagonists in these games are horrifying as they can pop up anytime, anywhere; and their screams constantly making my blood curdle. However, having way too many objectives can overwhelm the player with what to do; it also just doesn't make sense, story wise. Why does the character need to collect 7 anatomy parts anyway? The part I do get somewhat is collecting the red, blue, and orange papers with the masked red cloaked spirit chasing you (as it ties into the "Aka Manto" urban legend). Although, this game's story lacks as the mc doesn't have motive to do any of these things; other than being pressured to go inside a haunted, abandoned school by her peers/bullies. 

I feel like what could make "Aka Manto" work better (especially having it story driven), is having the mc being set in a lively but old school. The bullies from the beginning of the game can still play their part, just not outside an abandoned school. They'll be the reason why the mc will be using the 4th stall in the bathroom (and possibly to her doom). While using the bathroom, the mc notices that the 4th stall she's in has no toilet paper and groans in annoyance. Out of no where, the bathroom's light starts flickering as the mc hears footsteps coming closer to her stall. The light stops flickering but sees a red-ish hue shadow seeping under the stalls door. It asks "Do you want red paper.. Or blue paper?". Up to the player, they can answer either choice, type in a random color, or say "neither". Whatever answer the player chose can cause the mc to die in unique ways, but if quick enough can escape the Aka Manto. Once escaping out of the bathroom and away from the dark spirit, the mc notices that the school looks different. Dark, dirty, abandoned, and the atmosphere much heavier. Further on, the mc will begin to realize that she's been dragged into the netherworld in which resembles her school and must find her way back to her realm. To do so, she'll have to aid some of the lost souls who'll offer guidance, run and hide from dark spirits, and survive Aka Manto.

We all know the premise: The stars and habitable planets vanished. The Quiet Rapture left humanity clinging to space stations and barren moons. But I’ve always been bothered by the physics of it. Matter doesn’t just disappear.
​After re-playing the game and staring into the grain, I’ve developed a theory I call "Cosmic Biomass Inversion."
​1. The Rapture was a "Blender Event"
The central question of Iron Lung isn't "where did the stars go?", but "where did the blood come from?"
My theory: The stars and planets weren't deleted. They were processed.
The Quiet Rapture was a moment of instant entropy or cosmic digestion. Billions of living beings and lush ecosystems were ground down in a split second and teleported/deposited as raw biomass (blood) onto the nearest gravity wells—the barren moons like AT-5.
The space stations survived not because they were lucky, but because they were inedible. They are the plastic wrappers left over after the meal. When we sail the blood ocean, we aren't just sailing a weird anomaly; we are literally sailing through the liquefied remains of human civilization.
​2. The Organism ("The Fish") is an Antibody, not a Shark
If the blood ocean is the result of a cosmic event, evolution didn't have time to create a predator like the one we see at the end.
So, what is it?
If we accept the ocean is "dead biomass," then the creature is a Macrophage.
In biology, macrophages are cells that hunt down and consume foreign debris and bacteria.
​The Ocean = The rotting body of the universe.
​The Iron Lung = A foreign bacterium / infection.
​The Fish = The immune system cleaning it up.
​It didn't attack us because it was hungry. It attacked us because we didn't belong in the "stomach" of the universe.
​3. The Eye and the C.O.I. Betrayal
The most terrifying part isn't the teeth; it's the eye. In a lightless ocean, why evolve an eye?
Because it watches. It implies a malicious intelligence behind the Rapture. The universe isn't just empty; it's hostile.
This leads me to believe the C.O.I. knew exactly what was down there. We weren't sent to map resources. We were a sacrifice. A probe sent to trigger the immune response and see what happens. We were bait for a god that lives in our own spilled blood.
​TL;DR: The Rapture liquefied the planets into the blood oceans. We are sailing through the soup of our ancestors. The "Fish" is just a white blood cell cleaning up the trash (us).

One of the brilliant things this game does is avoid killing the player. The initial fear of dying is what motivates the player not to get caught by the monster, but after going through it over and over, you eventually stop being scared. Constantly waiting for something to *eventually* happen to you but never actually fulfilling that fearful anticipation keeps you edge throughout the experience, instead of constantly having the game’s tension interrupted by a repetitive jumpscare after making a mistake. It also forces the player to have to be completely immersed in the dark during certain segments, keeping you from using the light to become comfortable with the environment. From what I remember, Thomas Eastwood possesses Andy and his friend Arthur possesses Claus, and Peter Pumpkin is a demon. After an accident in which Thomas's daughter knocked her brother into the lake because of the demon, their lives all spiralled out of control. Thomas blamed his daughter and suspected Arthur of trying to take his family for himself, so riddled with grief and anger burned their house down one Christmas day with everyone still in it. Absolutely off his rocker now, he blames it on Arthur and murders him with an axe. Realizing what he's done, he creates Andy's Apple Farm and makes a deal with the demon to have them live on in the game as it's characters, but the demon turns on him and makes him become Andy. This is why he wants you to "Save Us." 

Interestingly, the developers released another game called Rabbit Knight which secretly tells the aftermath of Thomas's actions where his daughter, the one who accidentally killed her brother, survived the fire. However the demon tracked her down and trapped her in the second chapter.

Suffice it to say the story is really interesting and the way these secrets are all hidden is really creative, requiring you to play the game in different combinations and sometimes even playing wrong in order to unlock them. I'm very excited for Chapter 2!

This game definitely follows the stereotypical "cute thing but horror" trope that's been rampant in the indie industry lately, but there's some genuine skill in how everything is presented/designed. Identifying early on that there's something lurking in the pipes for example makes the player super nervous around each one, in which the developer perfectly places a bunch of open pipes in spots you have to walk past or grab an item near. On top of that, the concept of having to tie up the puppets is basically a more active version of the Crimson Heads from Resident Evil Remake, which is brilliant. It creates a constant anxiety and stress in knowing that, if you don't tie up an enemy, you'll have to deal with them should you come back through an area. And with lots of backtracking due to puzzles, that's a constant risk the player has to balance considering the duct tape is a limited resource. 

On top of the actually really strong sound design, the manic voices of the puppets, proper resource management that encourages the player to explore, and proper shooting gameplay that puts you face to face with the enemies, this could be a fantastic game if it's finished. Honestly though, it's just refreshing to have an indie horror game that isn't just walking around/hiding until a big jumpscare happens. I understand it's a popular form of gameplay in the horror genre these days, but it's nice to have a game where you actually have to fight back and manage resources to survive. It's sad that such a basic concept is pretty rare.

Or does the game celebrate the *developer's* choices, rewarding the player for choosing what the developer thinks is the right answer?" It's probably just me, I've never been fond of these kinds of games, it always felt like a litmus test on whether I share a mind with another human, like I'm being hunted for my capacity as a yesman.

One thing I find particularly interesting about this game is the living conditions of Mama Rabbit and her son, which strongly indicate that they are poor. Their house is very small and may even be an apartment, consisting of only three rooms, one of which triples as a living room, kitchen, and dining room. Their only food source appears to be a small refrigerator, and I guess whatever Mama Rabbit brings home from the bakery. A typical night's dinner is probably anything microwavable. They have no desks or drawers to set their lamps on, nor a stand for their primitive-looking television, which is probably Junior's only source of entertainment, because I didn't see any children's toys lying about. They have a built-in bathroom, but all they can bathe in is a washtub. (Not to bring any attention to Mama Rabbit's figure or anything, but overweight people sometimes use this instead of a regular bath because it's more accommodating for their size. It's possible that there WAS a bath in there at one point, but they had it removed and replaced with a washtub because it was too small, which probably cost them even more money.) The only bedroom in the house consists of a single bed that they most likely share. As Mama Rabbit walks into her house, she even comments on how late her hours are, leading me to believe she has to work overtime just so she can afford what little she has, including the ability to put her son through school.

For those who aren’t aware, roentgens are the international unit for radiation. Under different circumstances, total body exposure to 100 roentgens per hour can cause radiation sickness. You’ll feel absolutely horrible, both physically and mentally, but if the right precautions are taken, you’ll be fine. Exposure to anything up to 400 roentgens per hour will cause the body’s cells to disintegrate and half of all victims exposed to this much radiation will die.  

In 1986, when the Elephant’s Foot was discovered, it tapped out at *10,000 roentgens per hour.* Anybody exposed to it for longer than a minute was going to die.  

And Mark ran straight into it. 

Because he’s not a masochist, he just wants to see if his body can take it.

Just wanted to stress that this project was dedicated to all the liquidators, first responders, and support units that responded to the Chernobyl disaster. It was our goal to raise awareness for the people that contained the fallout, which is why we decided to go uncredited as developers and stay anonymous in the game. The focus of our game is squarely on them and the organizations that support those affected by this tragic moment in history. One such charity is Chernobyl Children International, who provides ongoing access to medical services and community support for children affected by the blast. Interesting radiation story:

During the nuclear bomb testing, they would often bring soldiers so they can “get used to” the bombs, they would be around a mile away from the bomb when it would detonate, in which they were instructed to cover their eyes as best they can to not be blinded by the blast.

Some covered their face with their arms, but ones using there hands claimed they could see the bone. They were then instructed to keep covering their face to wait for the heatwave, which they claim felt like opening a hot oven, but for 20 seconds.

After that they were told to uncover themself and watch the mushroom cloud form. Some were shell shocked while others were scared, and some even genuinely enjoyed it.

As expected many of them died the following years due to cancer, and some had fertility issues with their children. Of the 20-30 people there only in the 20-30’s, only 3 lived 20 years after the event.
It's insane how this group of men literally saved the world and we don't really recognize them internationally.

For those not in the know: the material that makes up the "Elephants foot" and the metallic looking stalactites scattered in the levels, is Corium. It's a mixture of nuclear fuel, insulation, concrete, nuclear moderator, and nuclear inhibitor materials, created during a core meltdown. Radioactivity from Corium is highly varied and unpredictable because of how these materials may be mixed, how they could interact, and because it is still being studied. Corium is always manmade, and accidentally created only 3 times: Chernobyl, Fukushima, and Three Mile Island. Deliberately made Corium is in laboratories in controlled conditions, for the purpose of study and research.

Not-so-fun fun fact.

The actual spaces they entered were only about five feet tall, and were separated into two identical floors. Dozens of steam suppression pipes filled the flooded rooms, making the pitch-black conditions even harder to navigate. While the "bubbler tanks" (emergency core cooling system component) were filled halfway during normal operation, fire water and ruptured circulation lines filled them up almost completely. These three men navigated a flooded, sprawling pipe maze, with molten nuclear fuel literally feet above their heads.

Even worse, the steam explosion theory was later proven to be false. The fuel reached the remaining layers of water (some remained after draining), and cooled harmlessly. They didn't need to be sent in there after all. 

We should never forget their bravery, nor the sacrifice of those sent to much more dangerous areas of Unit 4. They helped contain a catastrophe, and, thanks to their efforts, helped make nuclear power safer for all of us. The efforts of the liquidators, scientists, and engineers have guaranteed us that another RBMK explosion can never happen.

The scary thing is that Chernobyl was an avoidable disaster. Corners were cut in the construction of the facility and reactor, it was very poorly made. Safety violations occurred and protocols were unattended to before the meltdown. Nuclear energy is very safe and clean. It creates minimal pollution and is relatively low risk WHEN TAKEN SERIOUSLY. When not taken seriously, disaster occurs. It could have very easily been avoided if the proper precautions had been taken to make the reactor run properly. Laziness and half-assed work were the downfall of Chernobyl. And in the disasters wake, we created a horrific instance of man's most volatile manmade subtsance: Corium. It is still eating through the floor and concrete sarcophagus of the reactor to this day

An analysis of Mark's battle strategy…
 
     After an in depth analysis of this video and even more Mark’s request I needed inspiration to critique his battle style. 
I decided to turn to Sun Tzu’s The Art Of War. After reading cover to cover I found numerous incompetent misjudgment, and impulsive stupidity. Starting with basic formation strategies, and planning.
     Mark chose a “block” or “in line” formation to attack. This is most commonly recognizable from the civil war or pre modern warfare. Best for ranged attacks with non fully automatic rifles to simulate rapid fire by having each line of soldiers take turns firing, and ducking down to reload. However Mark selected this for a mass Guerilla melee warfare which quite frankly is an affront to the god of war Athena. Not only was it luck based it relied on strength with troops who had everything but. His duck platoon had higher attack rate, better concealment ability, and even moderately comparable speed. A better tactic would have been a distraction of about 10% of his troops in a reverse arrow formation to surround the block formation of the zombie horde. Along the distance to the battle use 30% for scattered ambushes, formatted to isolate, and execute small clusters of zombies, all groups holding parts of 50% as backup for each group to take out any following zombies who might have seen the ambush
     Once the numbers have been weakened and the horde is close enough to the 10% have what remains of the 70% ambush teams to flank the horde, with the last 20% funneling the sides out to flatten, and divide the hoard. This will take advantage of the duck’s numbers, and most valuable physical assets.
     Next is the war of the mind. This is an easy win as zombies already lack brain function, and ducks are known to be smarter, and more intuitive than most water dwelling birds. This allows for better local and on the fly strategy not to mention being “battle ducks” it implies previous field training. The zombies will be over confident seeing a lone horde of ducks secretly amassing only 10% of the duck’s full forces. Even more a conflict of emotion will befall the hordes as some worry about their slowly decreasing number while those closer to the center maintain confidence allowing for them to fall into the trap like lemmings. A divide of panic and overconfidence will brew to cause internal conflicts being waged on top of the slaughter that will befall the poor zombie hordes. This strategy titans over Mark's pitiful strategy of… Jack shit. He showed his weakness in leadership upfront with formation giving the zombies righteous confidence as they rush a block of weak and defenseless ducks with no plan. The best strategy was the predictable “flank em” maneuver that was not pre planned, and was never even fully completed resulting in an absolute atrocity of war strategy that I was offended by just watching.
     Please mark. Never join the military. You are a danger to your platoon, squadron, or otherwise.

     Before someone says something, this was written as a joke, just for fun.

SPOILERS





The world Cruelty Squad takes place in has removed death from the cycle of life. There is no true death any more, people "die" but they come back to life because death simply doesn't exist anymore, at least not how we know it. When you kill people and restart a level, it's not like going back in time and trying again, those people canonically died and came back to life when you do the level over again. The game's "main message", in a manner of speaking, is about the philosophy that life has no meaning if it goes on forever. Death gives meaning to life as much as life gives meaning to death, each is pointless without the other. The "true" ending to Cruelty Squad involves your character bringing true death back into the cycle of life, making life have meaning and truly worth living again.

The thing that makes this feel like a horror game are how easily the game strips you of comfort. I always check the back of my car before I get in, I don't walk around after dark unless at least two people know where I'm at, and I make sure all the doors I can lock are locked. I've worked terrible fast food jobs where I've been harassed by coworkers, and I've been yelled at by a customer until my manager had to get involved. That's the reality of working night shift as a woman in a customer service job. 

That's why this game is so disarming; the danger compounds with the high-pressure environment and uncomfortable situations. You can't just quit. You can't just run away. You're forced to work alone, unprotected, while people stare creepily at you from across the lobby. You can't always take safety precautions if you want to keep your job.
As someone who's trying to escape Retail Hell, I can confirm that you'd be expected to put the store's closing procedures above your own safety!

(in bob's storytelling voice) Bob's story transcripted

Once upon a time, there was a brave young man. Let's call him, "Flark." Flark needed to rescue his friends who were morons, and Flark's bravery knew no bounds. He was brave beyond all reason. Almost insane, you could say, how brave he was. Flark embarked upon a journey to rescue his first friend by walking awkwardly for a long time. Luckily, Flark's biceps and shoulders are literally the strongest things in the universe. He's able to carry, say a dead body, out in front of him like it's a dirty diaper. Doesn't want it to touch anything, but needs to carry it very carefully so as to not spill any of the poopies and/or dead body parts.

Flark's quest seemed to be coming to a rather successful end, unless he's an idiot too and doesn't know how this works.

Flark truly was the bravest of them all, but boy, was he stupid. Flark found a totem, and ran expeditiously back to Stonehenge, rather proud of himself; ignoring the fact that he had completely fucked up the first time and giving himself credit for doing it right even though it took more than one try.

Flark never did give up. He ran jauntily back to Stonehenge, not moving his arms at all. Too much muscle. Flark paid no mind to whatever friend he may have forgotten. Nobody asked for a check in on Glade.

—

The monster toyed with Flark, knowing that all he wanted was to be put out of his misery and refusing to give him the only thing he truly desired. Flark shot his stupid gun fruitlessly at the monster repeatedly, loading more shells and firing them, knowing in his heart the absolute and utter futility of his actions.

Flark stepped into a spiky tree trap. His bravery sustained him. Flark was nigh unkillable—and, an asset here to forth considered a good thing by most humans—but in Flark's quest to end his suffering, his unkillable nature was really most frustrating. He almost could feel himself healing as he wandered aimlessly through the woods. Flark's mind said repeatedly, "Please! End this!" but his troll said, "Not today."

The monster taunted Flark, knowing he couldn't even move. Flark's dying thoughts wandered as they often did to the ship of Theseus. Was he even still Flark? How do you decide who a person is? Maybe he was just a stranger he'd never met, dying alone in the woods.

the reason that cam stalling works on some animatronics and not others in UCN is because some aren't designed to be affected by the cameras. In the original FNAf, looking at animatronics on the cams slowed them down, that was a game mechanic. Cam stalling is just exacerbating that mechanic. But in UCN, some animatronics are designed not to be affected by the cameras, just like some aren't affected by the heater or the noise. I wouldn't say it's a glitch necessarily, but it is pushing a mechanic to its ultimate so I guess it's up to interpretation.

This is the story of a man named "Mark". Mark worked in his house, where he was a YouTuber by the name of "Markiplier." Mark's job was simple. He sat at his desk, playing video games and making videos. He played whatever games his audience wanted. Whatever they wanted to see him play, Mark did. This is what Mark did every day of every month of every year. And though others might find it tedious and soul-rending, Mark relished every game he was requested to play, as though he had been made exactly for this job. And Mark was happy.
And then one day, something very peculiar happened. Something that would forever change Mark. Something the internet would never quite forget. Mark had been recording a video for nearly an hour, when he got several hundred notifications from others about a new game release. Nobody had asked so much for one game. Never in all his years of YouTube had this happened; this complete surge of requests. Something was very clearly wrong. Shocked, Mark decided to look up this game, trying to see what the want for this game is. But as he found the game, he saw it was a re-release of a different game. Nevertheless, Mark downloaded the game, and started to play.

And it just happens again... and again... and again.

I think that what she meant by that is that everytime we die the wormhole doesn't reset time, we simply jump to another universe. By jumping to a new universe (either by dying or by using the portable wormhole generator) the old one we just left still remains, which means that we leave the colonists of the old universe to die. But unlike Mark and us (the captain) the colonists don't go to a new universe when they die, they simply remain dead. This is what we're seeing here, the corpses of multiple colonists from across multiple universes.

I just had a weird image of an alien explorer ship of other species cruising along, mapping the stars, when suddenly one of them spots a strange shape. At first they think it is an asteroid, and they cautiously drift closer to try and see if it leads to a larger asteroid belt. However, a quick scan identifies it as a human body... just... floating. They would find this curious and drift towards it... and slowly, their windows would fill with a view of three more corpses. And then 10 more bodies. And then 40... 60... 100... 126... 134.... 200... and counting. Clouds of blood expand from some of the corpses. Others look contorted in off way, like they had been bashed against walls before being thrust into space. They would wonder what had caused shuch havoc, and looming out of the ghostly light of the stars is a huge, colossal, jagged shape. It is a dark human ship, lifeless and titanic in size, a grim obelisk marking a ring of aging death. They would look beyond the ship, gripped with utter terror and wonder what kind of monster, what horrific cosmic beast could have created such merciless destruction.

*And you* will never look back, continuing to blindly feel out the paths that twist and turn in convoluted but vaguely familiar patterns, slowly mapping out the wormhole. As you go on, your morals will begin to gray as you become numb to horrors you have seen, the things you have felt, the deaths you have tasted, the things you have built and seen destroyed, the wrongs you have done. You will become focused on one thing: escaping this hell, attempting the last resort: rebooting the whole-ass universe. You need a reset to erase the blood that stains the stars, the smoke and ash that smears your face and clothes, the film of horror and grief that has settled upon your all too-seeing, baby gray eyes. The only thing you can hold onto are your memories... and Mark.

And you will hardly notice the creatures that look at you like a monster.
That look at you like *a god.*
And you will carry on.

The first half of the song is a variation of a children’s prayer, the “Now I lay me down to sleep, I pray my lord my soul to keep” one. The guy who popularized the prayer, Monk Preston, said it every night before he went to bed until the age of 18-19. He also said he wasn’t sure about thinking he’d die in his sleep, every single night of his youth. What’s interesting to me is that the prayer isn’t to make sure you don’t die but instead for when you die, almost like it’s unavoidable.

The second half is a variation on the children’s song “There are Four corners to my bed”, which is similar but the 4 “angels” are different. “One to watch and One to pray, Two to to guide me through the day”. In this version, only 3 angels are mentioned: “One to watch and one to pray, and One takes my soul away”. I have no idea why.

I didn't mind Security Breach when I watched it at first, but with every revisit I realize that the older games were so much better. It's amazing how much of what makes a FNAF game is just....missing. The older games managed to nail simple yet terrifying mechanics and used claustrophobic environments to their advantage. Bigger isn't always better. Security Breach has some good going for it but it feels like they nerfed it by making it more kid friendly and marketable.

Sister Location was always a really impressive expansion from the previous games. There was a much longer wait from FNAF 4 to this one, and that combined with what I'm assuming is a higher budget really helps makes this one stand out. There's just so much MORE to this game; more mechanics, more voice acting and dialogue, more story, and I think all these expansions were made in the right direction. Revisiting these games has unfortunately really showed how... detached Security Breach feels, not so much that it's not connected to the previous story very much, but how different it is in its tone and atmosphere. I think SB really failed to capture what made FNAF so captivating, it had its moments, definitely, but it doesn't really hold up well to the previous games despite how much "simpler" they are in their mechanics and presentation.

Tips for everyone here: 
To beat Funtime foxy, do as follows:
Flash once, and see if the room is clear. If you don't see Foxy, run for 6-7 steps. Stop, flash, and check. If foxy is there, count to 7. Flash again and check if he's still there. When the room is clear, repeat. Run for 6-7 steps, flash, check, and if the room is clear, run another 6-7 steps and repeat until you finish the room. Wait and count to 7 if foxy is there and flash to check again.

tips!

- when springtrap stares through the window, you can still lure him to cam 02 if you're quick enough.
- when springtrap is in a room with vent access, preemptively seal it.
- at 12am, no phantom animatronics can spawn apart from foxy and springtrap cannot enter vents.
- when you need to reboot the systems, never hit reboot all. it gives springtrap ample time to reach the office while you're still waiting. instead, do it one at a time while luring him away in between reboots. the audio is your top priority, followed by the ventilation and finally the cameras.
- *this is not a question of the fastest way to reboot every system. it is a question of the best way to keep springtrap away from you for the entire night.* before leaving a reply, ensure you've read this bullet point at least twice. it will be on the test.
- do you hear the whistle at 15:40? it plays when springtrap is in cams 05-04-03, and plays distinctively louder when he's in cams 02-01 and in the hallway to your office. it also plays when phantom freddy is in the hallway, or phantom chica is in the office.
- phantom freddy can only spawn at the top of every hour, and he's guaranteed to spawn at 4am if he hasn't already jumpscared the player.
- to avoid getting jumpscared by phantom foxy, don't look at him and just open the camera monitor.
- there is a flat 1/7 chance for springtrap to ignore an audio lure. it's just good to know so you aren't caught off-guard when it happens.
- once springtrap gets to cam 01, he can't be lured to any other cameras. the only thing you can do is keep him there.

this advice applies to all nights, but is focused on night 6.

Marks constant mention of scars actually brings attention to a  really good point about analog horror and just horror in general—the fact that people with scars or deformities or disabilities ARE constantly demonized. Horror media does use the appearance of real life people to portray a feeling of unsettlement or terror to the audience.

In fact, horror media relies on the images of disabled people so much that you can't remove that from the horror genre without uprooting almost the entire genre with few exceptions. This isn't me saying "oh we need to cancel the horror genre as a whole" (???) Or whatever but just a fact to be conscious of when you interact with horror.

Lets take a second to appreciate how unique ISWM is as a piece of media and entertainment...

It's a POV choose your own adventure set in space where you're the captain of a ship forced into a time loop, trying desperately to save your crew over and over–or so we thought. Each "reset" after a death is actual us jumping into a the body of an "us" from another universe, ultimately leaving the ship of the previous universe completely hopeless. And that's only the premise of PART ONE of this adventure. While taking more creative liberty with the whole time loop and universe jumping concept, part two still follows a great narrative: our recklessness leads to universes overlapping, and we have to find a solution before the paradox destroys the multiverse.

I personally can't think of any cinematic experience that even comes close. The storytelling was clever and emotional, and it even seamlessly ties back into the bigger Markiplier lore for the dedicated fans. I'm glad I got to share this adventure with everyone here <3

Relevant information for "How Fish Is Made":

First and most importantly, Lixian is not kidding with his warning before the "musical number".  There are many disturbing and disgusting images present, including the putrefaction of a human brain.  You have been warned.

Trypophobia, or "fear of holes", is the fear of high-contrast patterns, most often patterns in places that look jarring or off-putting to human sensibilities.  The trypophobia segments are at 35:30 to 36:02 and a long one from 42:37 to 45:53.

The parasite that eats a fish's tongue is a real thing:  Cymothoa exigua, the tongue-eating louse.  To be exact, it doesn't actually eat the tongue; it removes the tongue and replaces it, then subsists on the mucus of the fish's mouth.

As you might imagine, the game only loosely resembles actual fish processing.  Those trypophobia-inducing areas with fish in holes, for instance, are strictly there for the squick factor.

Hi Mark! The mop and the bucket blocking you is a reference to a joke we have in Spain about mothers (traditionally, nowadays dads too) getting really angry when someone steps on recently cleaned floor, and refusing to let you get into that room/hallway.

The first game, although I'm not from Spain, speaks a lot about some of the Country's history, as it references Francisco Franco's anti-communist dictatorship. Even the name of the Game, "Rojo" which means red, was a common name used by fascists to discriminate/identify communists or people that could be considered enemies. During this period of the Country's history you could be chased, killed or imprisoned for speaking your mind, or even only being suspected of being a Communist. If you are interested in more information you should read about the Spanish Civil War, and about the story of "La República" (a socialist-esque totalitarian government that ruled over the country before Francisco Franco came into the picture).

About the game, it appears the person's missing friend, who probably was of alt-right political beliefs, became mentally deranged and started carrying out horrible acts and experiments on "reds" (people he probably suspects are communists, leftists or liberals) because of his adoration of the figure of Francisco Franco (represented in the multiple depictions and pictures of the Dictator around the house, and the flag that Spain used as it's national flag during the period Francisco Franco was in power).

Very interesting game, as normally Mark doesn't play games that carry or talk about actual historical facts.

As I've said, I am not from Spain, but from Argentina, and there's a lot about this period in History that I don't know, if you are as much of a nerd for history as me, you should totally read more on this topics.

Thx for your time, kisses

SOME HISTORICAL AND CULTURAL CURIOSITIES ABOUT THE FIRST GAME:

- ROJO (Red) it's how the spanish communists were named in the dictatorship

- Generalísimo was how it was called Franco, the dictator of that time.

- You can see Spains Flag with a Black eagle on one of the walls: thats the Flag of the "Falange", and it has the same connotation as the nazi Flag (so you can understand it)

- The Black and White TV shows a documental of the past, in the dictatorship time

- The funeral that you can see in the other TV it's actually Franco's funeral

- catholithsm  was really important in Spain, thats why the great number of Jesus and virgin María that are on the pictures. Also we can watch on the walls some propaganda from the dictatorship and pictures of Franco and King Juan Carlos (now ex King of the country)

- The four notes on the piano to unlock the door are the first four notes of the Spanish Anthem

Some notes from a seasoned Observation Duty player:

The gongs ascertain to the time (one gong is 1am, two gongs is 2am, etc) - the goal is to last until 6am FNAF style, so the gongs just remind you of how long you've got left and add some ambience.

The alert warning you of your impending doom means that there are three anomalies that haven't been reported, and it's game over once there are four active. The alert only appears once, even if later in the game you reach the same critical point, so use that warning wisely and use that report button! You had the right idea banging out reports like missing/moving objects in rooms with lots of small items which could be easy to miss; there are no penalties for logging false reports.


HOWEVER, the reports pend a lot faster in this version, but they take longer in the earlier games. If you play any of those, be careful not to spam the reports and to save them for when you're semi-certain you've spotted an anomaly, I can't tell you how many times I lost because there was already a report pending and I spotted something too late that wrecked me.

Look out for the camera malfunctions, those are easy to miss. Sometimes entire rooms will disappear, so count the rooms every so often to make sure they're all still there.

The "other" anomaly at 28:50 was the floor tiles, they changed from the usual small squares to larger squares. Very easy to miss, lucky report!

The death at 30:57 was caused by distortion, that's a hard death to avoid since you'd assume it would be logged as a camera malfunction, but by the time you go to log another report it's too late - just one of those things you learn as you play. Abyss presences are essentially black holes that spread across a room, and if they aren't reported quickly it's an automatic game over like the distortion. They're pretty easy to spot, they grow quite fast.

Getting all the way to 5am is actually pretty impressive on only your second run, so well done! Observation Duty is simple but surprisingly hard and tense. I hope you play more of it in the future, especially the first game, I have a soft spot for that one since I watched the Game Grumps play it which got me to buy the game myself. The third game is free roam, which would make for a good video I think, it looks way scarier since you're actually in the house!

This game actually takes advantage of a perceptual phenomenon called "Change blindness", when even if there are huge changes or small changes, the observer does not notice a different due to not seeing the picture for a split second, for example if it were to turn to a black screen or another area for just a few moments, unless they're actively focusing something specific

This game does do an excellent job at envoking a feeling of helplessness. You never know what moves will kill you. Very unlike most horror games which will tell you how to survive, via notes left around, audio logs, or just text on the screen. Add to the fact that home invasion is a real life threat, and it makes for a chilling horror game that makes people freeze.

This game does a lot of things right. The atmosphere is a big part of that. Probably the worst part about it though is how it’s perfectly reasonable. Parents leave teenagers alone all the time. Home invasions happen all the time. That little view of feet going upstairs while you watch TV could actually happen. We’ve all missed something obvious while distracted. That’s what’s so terrifying about this. We can all see this exact scenario happening to us personally. It’s a different experience to say a game that focuses on some strange supernatural entity. We all know the darkness demon isn’t real but a home invader, that could happen right now. This experience hits us on a primal level of our privacy being invaded. Absolutely perfectly crafted experience that really preys on your paranoia, and a pretty reasonable paranoia at that.

Anyways, I know no one asked but I have a home alone story for y’all.

Okay so this happened I’d say about a month or two after my family and I had moved into a new house. This house had, and I kid you not, a mile long driveway. It is in the middle of the woods with no neighbors. I was around 12 or 13 when this happened. I was sitting in my room while my sister, brother, and parents were all out running errands. It was currently 8 PM and they left at 6 PM, so I was hoping they were going to be home any minute, when my two dogs started barking. I was confused so I looked out the window to see a black figure with a flashlight emerging from the woods. My heart skipped a fucking beat. I grabbed my dogs and put them inside with me, locked my doors and windows, grabbed my knife, because why not, and ran into our “secret” room, which was in my brothers closet. One of the walls pushed out and there was a fairly sized room there which the old owners probably illegally grew drugs in but none of my business. My dogs were very stressed but I gave them beef jerky to distract them. Mind you, they are both over 90 pounds. Someone knocked on the door so I texted my mom about what was happening, but my phone had no service. I heard like digging in the front yard? You know when you have a shovel and you stick it in the ground and pull it out? Yeah, that. Anyway, my parents got home about 45 minutes later of me sweating and freezing at every sound. We checked the ring camera and it was a hooded drunk man who had escaped jail and was running through the woods. He buried a fork in our front yard, and left. Scariest moment in my life

This reminds me of a situation from a few years back when I was 19.

Was gaming late (as in like 2am-3am) and decided I was thirsty, so I left the office where I'd put my PC, opened the sliding door and just took a step ahead when I heard a thud. Looked ahead properly and here I am, with 5 people I don't know staring back at me. I froze for a second, staring at them, then jumped backwards, closing and locking the sliding door while calling the police and the neighborhood watch.
Then they scramble and are out of the window (which they'd completely removed) and were gone in seconds. I was never so freaked out in my life.

Turns out the cleaning lady we'd hired had been part of a group where she'd loosen windows so these people could completely remove the glass while the home owners are either out or asleep, then they come in quietly and rob the place.
They'd even taken my dad's phones from right next to his head on the bedside table... he's terrified to even think what could have happened had he woken up. We got lucky that I got thirsty when I did, it stopped them from stealing more, but it's still a terrifying thought that all that happened and he never woke up. I heard nothing at all... just walked in from gaming to see 5 unfamiliar faces in my kitchen in the dark.

Saiko is an incredibly in depth AI and the creator happily shows it off on their youtube channel. I suggest to all interested that you play the game a bit and then go to the channel and check it out. She almost feels alive with how she acts and treats the player.

Some tips:
____________________________________________________________________________
*1)* Pink text = Normal mode and Red text = Yangire
____________________________________________________________________________
*2)* You can calm Saiko through head pats if she's in the process of switching to Yangire. However, this can sometimes fail. 
____________________________________________________________________________
*3)* Locked rooms will have the numbers for the safe
____________________________________________________________________________
*4)* Keys can't be found in lockers
____________________________________________________________________________
*5)* Saiko can hear running and doors opening if near. It's best to open all doors and check them later
____________________________________________________________________________
*6)* It's a good idea to not creep around corners as the AI can camp corners (Example: 33:34)
____________________________________________________________________________
*7)* You can crouch through tripwires and glass. Crouching through glass will make noise though
____________________________________________________________________________
*8)* It's best not to use the infirmary key until you need it because Saiko can relock the room
____________________________________________________________________________
*9)* You can try running or using the power switch as a distraction if you want to move her away from a specific spot. Like the headmaster room for example
____________________________________________________________________________
*10)* If you get drugged and fall asleep while she is Yangire, she will instakill you. If you fall asleep while she's normal, she will kidnap you in the infirmary.

Please make more videos on this game. This game has become one of my all-time favorites. Btw I wouldn't recommend Yangire mode until you have  a good understanding of the game's mechanics and map knowledge

You can headpat her to calm her down I think, only on normal and hard mode.
Glass will harm you, but you can bypass this by either walking slowly or finding shoes. For some reason Saiko took your shoes.

The panic this game induces is like no other. Horror games are all about removing power from the player. As a result, multiplayer horror games are notoriously hard to pull off, as you'll always have the power of teamwork to balance tasks with. Not to mention, giving a player a gun, or any weapon in a horror game automatically empowers people. But GTFO gives you a gun, as if to empower you, then constantly threatens to remove that power through the starvation of ammo, health and material.

Unlike most good multiplayer horror games, which usually take a more classical approach to horror with jumpscares and creepy environments (like Phasmophobia), GTFO is truly, truly a psychological horror. It relies not on the idea that you *can* fight the monsters, it's that you absolutely *don't want to* . The monsters alone aren't scary. There's an induced fear of them brought on by resource attrition that triggers something different in our brain, giving us that reluctance we bring to each fight. It's telling us that we simply *can't* fight them, even if we very much can. 

Each of those white dots is a another potential resource vacuum, and each resource wasted is another potential foot in the grave. Something to invalidate all the care you put into your run up to that point. And there's something more scary about that, something almost instinctual, that's scarier than any single monster can provide.

And where multiplayer coop games live by teamwork, GTFO will kill you by it. A single mistake from one person cripples the entire team. Having that human factor *times four* only adds to that absolute dread of every encounter.  Even though you need your allies at your side, you know full well they can be your downfall. 

Work together, or die together. There couldn't be a more perfect tagline for this game than that.

Congratulations, Mark, after years playing horror games you finally summed up what horror is.

Degrence:
A feeling of pure, absolute euphoria, magnitudes better than what any drug other than Thalasin + can do. It is combined with the extreme satisfaction over everything, even the most mundane of things. Accompanied by a minor drop in blood pressure.

Humber:
Extreme confusion. The literal form of someone saying something so stupid that your brain hurts.

Nage:
A feeling of forced friendliness, to the point where it becomes psychotic.

Dorcelessness:
The best term that can describe this infamous emotion is literally 'nothing'. It's a giant void in the part of your mind that controls emotion. Numbness of the mind. Notice the flattened skull in the Dorcelessness portrait? That represents the figurative loss of the parts of your brain that trigger emotion, a part of your brain is gone.

Andric:
If normal cringe was being hit in the face with a paper ball, Andric is like being hit in the face with a nuclear bomb. It's like that pain you get when you hit your funny bone, but amplified by many magnitudes.

Varination:
The reason there are two portraits is to show different intensities. Varination 1 is like being frozen-in-fear. Like you are home alone and something breaks in the kitchen. Varination 2 is like you are bracing for something terrible to happen, like you are sinking back into yourself, just ready for it.

Ponnish:
The feeling you get when witnessing something that just destroys your soul. The best thing to compare it to is the sadness mixed with fear that a lot of Public Service Announcements give off. You just sink back upon being hit with something Ponnish-inducing.

Harfam:
It's like your brain can no longer comprehend the mere existence of itself and everything around it. Your brain just crashes.

Kyne:
Kyne is like you have suddenly and instantaneously acquired all knowable information in the universe at once. So much information that your brain just collapses in on itself. Equivalent to scoring an infinity on an IQ test.

Trantiveness:
An extreme connection to nature. The feeling that you have become one with nature, and this is reflected in the two Trantiveness portraits, which show human characteristics melted with various things in nature (First one represents a tree, second one represents a flower)

Teluge:
The feeling that you are going to die and/or everything will be annihilated. An extreme feeling of dread, to put it lightly.

Onlent:
Pure white-hot anger. The feeling like you must obliterate every single proton, neutron, and electron of someone or something. This emotion suppresses all others, and like primal instinct, results in you attacking whatever you feel Onlent towards.

Loric:
Similar to Dorcelessness, in a way. The pure neutrality of all emotions. To put it into an analogy: if all emotions were mapped on a coordinate grid, Loric will be dead in the origin point, or (0,0). You don't feel anything. You don't even feel as though you don't feel anything.

[REDACTED]:
The unlabeled emotion is not an emotion. It is a grim reminder to everyone regarding drug abuse. This leads me to believe that this commercial is not meant to advertise a product. It is a PSA. A drug abuse PSA. It shows what happens when you take the seriousness of drugs lightly, though the uncanny valley of the Thalasin + emotions...
