The word that you’re looking for is “Uncanny,” you know what this is but there is something about it that’s off. It’s actually a deep root for human’s fear of monsters.

Analog horror is *almost* scary, that’s where it’s so perfect. If you look at all of really good analog horror it doesn’t have much in the way of jumpscares or gore like traditional scare factors, where Mark says some of the videos fall flat is because they lean too hard on the “scary skinwalker comin to get youuu”. If you make it so your scary thing is completely normal, then you can trust the audience to make the rest of it scary. So when the final twitch happens the audience is like YEP SEE I KNEW SOMETHING WAS WRONG and then they feel that horrified validation that something is absolutely wrong and it’s been here this whole time. It’s taking advantage of the fear of the dark. “That small corner of my room is dark, there is absolutely someone or something standing in there and I cannot go to sleep but I won’t move or else it will get me”. If the corner started doing chippa chimp goofy stuff then you’d just tuck the covers up or call for someone. What makes that dark corner terrifying is that until it does something, you *cannot* look away.


You are not *allowed* to look away.



Keep looking.



Keep looking.

I was not expecting to get as emotional as I did watching Leshy's part. Definitely got a little misty eyed during it.

I'll admit, I got a little emotional at the Leshy part. I think of all the Scrybes, he was the best. Yes, he did some terrible things, but for one, the others were worse. Magnificus controlled and tortured those who were loyal to him in excess for seemingly no reason. P03 was obsessed with the Great Transcendence and cared not for the lives of anyone. Grimora may seem to be decently kind, but I feel that it masks an inner desire for death and the withering of all things, with a sunnier demeanor brought by the knowledge that it is inevitable. Of them all, Leshy was the only one who both understood and appreciated what they were doing. He was the only one who knew that Inscryption was a game meant to be experienced, and the only one who tried to make that happen. With Leshy an immersive and at least enjoyable story was being told, beyond the ambitions and obsessions of the other. Magnificus wanted knowledge and dominance over the game. P03 wanted to go beyond it. Grimora wanted to destroy it. Leshy only desired to play it. That's why his leaving is the saddest to me. He worked hard to honor the idea of the game, and only wants to enjoy it a little longer. It makes me sentimental. When he speaks in that last section it's almost like you're able to speak to the game itself, interacting with it directly. As he tries to keep the game going as it all collapses he speaks to that inner desire we all have as players just to have fun, to tap into joy and imagination and be free of the tribulations of the world, and the sadness that pervades us when it gets taken away. Stripped of everything, all Leshy wanted was what we wanted: to lose oneself in a good game. It's poetic really.
When he started reading Leshy's lines, I actually felt like I was about to cry. Mark's voice acting is phenomenal when you least expect it.

Some tips regarding killing scouts (no spoilers, don't worry):

- Scouts can be killed when they have their tentacles out.
- A charged melee from either the hammer or spear can kill a scout in one hit (if you hit the head).  The knife and bat can also kill a scout in one hit (if hit from the back of the head), but due to shorter range you will need to jump.
- If you touch a scouts feelers (tentacles), you have around 2 seconds to kill the scout before it goes blue and alerts everything.  This time varies depending on how close or far the feeler was from the scout.
- Once the scout is alerted and turns blue, it cannot be killed until after it screams.
- Scouts are not alerted by running.  Instead they will simply put their feelers back out.
- From what I know, scouts can only be alerted by gunshots, or from someone touching their feelers.  Because of this, you are able to sprint to get away from the feelers without alerting it.
- By following the feelers of a scout as they are retracting, you can get within melee distance without alerting it.  This allows for a silent melee kill.  If you touch a tentacle on the way in, referring back to a previous point, you have to kill it before the alerted (red) feeler touches the scout.  If all is going wrong, maybe just snipe it.

Knowing what to do regarding scouts will help, but will not make it easy by any means.  They're a difficult enemy to counter (when in groups).  When not in groups, it helps to remember that a dead scout and an awake room is generally better than the inverse.

"Bolthound? How did you get that out so soon?!" My theory is, Inscryption was always meant to have asymmetric gameplay, including in the "physical TCG" version. One player (you) has to obey card costs, but your cards take immediate effect. The other player (Scrybe or otherwise) can _ignore card costs entirely,_ but their cards are delayed by a turn (they have to play their cards into the "arrow row" first, and then move into the active row one turn later). In theory, P03 could flood his board with Double Gunners, Leshy could fill his board with Urayuli, etc, but they _don't,_ not because the rules forbid them to, but because they're personally obligated to create _challenging but fair_ battles for the player to experience, to have the game be _beatable._

Presumably, the "Scrybe player" (both ingame and in the TCG version) has a limit on _how many_ cards they can queue per turn, with the number increasing as the match continues, but nothing's stopping them from having a *_FLYING UYARULI_* as their turn-one play except for the spirit of fairness. And the Scrybes _want_ you to be able to win in the end, to reach the end of the game. (Though there's been reports on /r/inscryption of players having their 2000/2000 Ouroboros angled and watching as the game dutifully spawns 2,000 teeth on your side of the scale, crashing the game with too many physics objects... Hey, nothing said Leshy _can't_ be a dick once in a while for the lulz.)

The gameplay is so fascinating to me because it seems to be a recreation and corruption of the way children explore their world for the first time. As the player, you aren't given any verbal or written instructions. The absence of dialogue only furthers the experience as one of raw emotion, you're not told what to feel, you just feel it. You don't even know what it is, and you just experience it. You experiment with everything, pulling and pushing, often in destructive or unintentionally violent ways, like a very curious young child. It's undeniable things get harmed in your way whether you intend them to or not. Every change in color and noise captures your attention because they're new, often terrifying; you're put in a position to pay attention to everything minute, as though you were an easily entertained infant, in order to progress the game. 

It's the primal fear of the unknown but not with a void or nothingness, but with an new world functioning by foreign rules that you're trying desperately to learn about, like what happens after you're born. The style of the game is like the epitome of surreal horror and dark surrealism, in the likes of the Grinch's Paraphernalia/Dr. Seuss's darker works, Pink Elephants on Parade, and the more menacing aspects of Salvador Dali's work. Just a very interesting design, I love the developmental choices.

My analysis of the game:

The Smiley Demon is not actually malevolent, it is trying to help him. In every nightmare we see the boy lose something (the ball getting stolen, the bunny dropped in the lake, the dog running away) and every time the Demon sees the boy's sadness and nods to the player as if to say 'Alright, let's deal with this.'
That is why, whenever he wakes up, he has the thing back he lost. And then the Demon gently lulls him back to sleep so it can find more trauma to fix.

The three chapters each seem to be about certain uncomfortable issues. I don't know what chapter 3 is about, but I have a pretty good idea about 1 and 2.

The first chapter seems to be about sensory overload. You will notice, even though all the toys tend to look scary and menacing, he doesn't actually seem scared of them most of the time. It is only when they all start making flashing lights and cacaphonous noises that the kid starts to panic, or when they are actively trying to attack him. It is also when the noises are loudest that he gets his recurring visions of being impaled. The chapter ends with him finding his ball, a toy that is neither loud, nor flashy, making it the antithesis of all the other toys in his dream, and he tellingly manages to narrowly avoid his promised impalement by grabbing the ball and waking up once he has it, showing that the ball is safe for him, as opposed to the torturous overload of the other toys.

The second chapter can best be described to be about gluckschmerz (deriving pain or discomfort from other peoples' happiness). Throughout the entire chapter, the denizens of the smiley bunny land are either trying to punish you for being happy, or are themselves getting punished for their happiness. You try to feed the bunnies to make them happy, only for the monster bunny to devour them. You actively have to make many of the heart children unhappy to the point of death to survive the third bunny monster. The smiley part has an angry smiley that kills anyone that tries to pass while being happy, and in the end, in order to pass, you have to make him happy, only to make him sad again. And the end of chapter 2 has you rob the happiness of the three smiley heads and literally break their hearts. The puddle sees you rip him apart and mess with his insides, the fire bunny has you kill the tiny imps for his pleasure, only to burn him, and then dismantle his skeleton when he tries to protect himself. And the sawbox has you stop the smiley from enjoying his sadistic experiments on the bunnies, only for the bunnies to turn out just as sadistic as him.

The third chapter, I couldn't really find a coherent theme in the events. Possibly something about how nature is scary, or about bullying and wanton cruelty from the denizens of the dream, but really, that all feels like a reach in a way my other chapter interpretations do not. 

However, the end portion of the chapter feels like their own seperate theme from whatever the rest of the chapter tried to convey. He reunites with the dog, but where he would ordinarily wake up, as with chapter 1 and 2, this time the dog is taken away again, into the red void. He follows, and ends up falling endlessly among broken, mangled versions of his own visage, ending with popping open his head to find pictures of his ball, bunny, and dog. That's when you rewind the whole thing into a maelstrom of bits and pieces from all three dreams, and then wake up to find your ball, bunny, and dog safe and sound. And that is also where we get the twis ending of the boy being a grown man, lying drugged up in a puddle of his own fluids. That whole bit seems to just be about the grim reality that the happiness that the Smiley Demon brought him is all in his head, a junkie's pipedream. The broken visages of himself shows the truth of him being a broken individual, the drawings of his things are depictions of his happy memories. And the ending where he pounds on the window and draws a smiley face seem to imply that he is trapped in his own misery and pursuit of his childhood innocence. The fact that the smiley drawing flashes into the Smiley Demon for a moment also implies that the Demon is, indeed, his own creation. A small piece of his mind that tirelessly attempts to fix himself, even though he is irrevocably broken.

But those are just my thoughts. If you have any other ideas, it would be cool to hear them, and I am especially curious if anyone has an idea of what chapter 3 could symbolize that is in line with my theories.

to summarize everything I've seen and heard people say:
- save point disabling should have only been a side objective to re-enable them as soon as you choose to stay (the rumored Vanny spawn system should have been also been tied to this), or been for a one life only mode.
- autosaves should have been set to occur after defeating a boss fight/survival section depending on difficulty (and balanced accordingly)
- security drones are probably fine, but should have been HEAVILY affected by the Fazerblaster and Camera (i/e former kills on low difficulties like in the Fazerblaster arena, latter only stuns on all difficulties)
- animatronics (Roxy in particular) should have had 2 objectives on how to deal with them; the current "destroy" option marked in the quest log, and a secret "save" option that can only be done following in-game notes and collectables (could even be heavily tied into the Fazerblaster and missing Glamrock Bonnie)
- Party Pass drones shouldn't despawn until you're out of sight, if at all

The fear and hesitation that follows alongside the first voyage of any ship; spacefaring or seafaring, is immense. The anxiety brought upon by the induced paranoia of unpreparedness is something that follows every member of a crew. The chance that the ship springs a leak and begins to sink, the off-chance that something big attacks the ship...mutiny, sea/space sickness, and the ever developing fear of being lost in a place you yourself are not familiar with.

Fear itself is a powerful tool in the hands of no one.

And what it inspires in people whosoever's hearts are either hardened or weakened, is something terrible indeed. This preview shows that example very well, as the chaos of multiple intervening voices becoming more and more panicked show that very same growing anxiety. Doubt sets in, and everything comes to the Captain of the vessel to bring things to a head. To bring together the crew that until that point, had been teetering at the edge of tearing themselves apart.

And though they might succeed in their journey, they will not arrive at their destination without taking with them the fear, and memory of those who died along the way.

"O' Captain, My Captain", indeed.

In Reality: It’s actually not.

The watching smile, to me, feels like a representation of sadism, schadenfreude. Toying with the kid, keeping things out of reach, like the real life bully with the ball. Constantly taking, leading on, then torturing the child. This could be how he sees others, an underlying distrust in strangers that they may just want to watch him suffer for fun, for a laugh. Notice how all suffering is either played for laughs by others, or just outright painless. The dream characters are just desensitized to the horrible torture and death around them. The sad big head in happy smile head land is the only truly sad and vulnerable, taking the injustice out on all of the "happy normal people". But the kid, now with his happy mask broken, is able to console the big head after it's thrown through an emotional rollercoaster.

Maybe the kid has witnessed the harshness of reality, felt scorned by society at large. Internalizing this idea of everyone living a false, lunatic happiness. Where everything bad is good, and just being himself makes him a target to more suffering.

coming back after having played the game for myself, it is amazing just how effective he is at getting through the game despite his many misplays. Yes, knowledge is a factor, and as much as i want to blame him for not knowing the mechanics of each boss phase, i cannot. What i can blame him for on the other hand is his strange deck building choices, and inability to see the swarming potential he accidently stumbles into. 

His cockroach is a great example of sigil synergy, and he never fully realized it. After the initial summon, it is effectively a better cat. sacrifice it, get the card and its cost back for free, play it again, sacrifice, rinse and repeat until he is out of spaces or cards that need sacrifice, all while also outputting damage, something the cat cant do on its own. That isnt even mentioning the secret limitation on cat that the cockroach he built ends up completely bypassing.

Final death card COULD have been FREE, thanks to a pelt showing up as cost option, yet markiplier somehow thinks 1 blood is a better cost.

With multiple warren cards on top of cockroach, tributing should have never been a factor for anything but 3 or 4 blood cost.

The single biggest mistake Markiplier was consistently making is not knowing when to draw from the deck compared to squirrels. He would have no potential sacrifices anywhere in hand or board, build a deck full of sacrifice-needing cards, yet draw from the deck without a solid offense/defense. Maybe if he had some freebies in the deck, i could understand the gamble, but the only cards that fit that description were pelts; things that could at best wall up, but never give blood. Squirrels can wall just as effectively as low tier pelts considering the offensive pressure he was under with most instances of the poor choice.

With all that said, the only chance markipler had to get past speedrunner trapper was to use the knife more wisely, getting an early lead that he only needed to secure 1-2 extra points through FLY DEFENSE (yet another mistake in his assessment of win conditions) grizzlies.

During night Bigfoot gets a bonus to attack, in the day he gets a bonus to healing. Turning off your lights actually makes you harder to see. Smells and noise attracts him more than you realize. He can literally see the direction of a sound from half way across the map! The thumping is him weakening trees and gathering weapons. If you stay quiet you can hear what sounds like rope twisting, that means a tree trap is near by. It is better to place those hazards at his feet and shoot them, than it is to try to hit him with it or detonate (gas cans, generators, dynamite, etc.) Before you trek a long distance, wait for day light. The map is randomly generated. It uses the same land mass but locations get randomly placed for each new game. His hideout is at the marble caves.

The other endings in "Good Boy".  The story remains the same until you get the knife:

Ending 1:  Follow the blood trail to the cat in your room.  Stab it.  The trail now leads to the cat in the living room. Kill that one and the door to the kitchen opens.  Kill your mother and your "grandmaw" calls you back, then calls 911 -- to bring more people for you to kill for "our master's heart".

Ending 3:  Follow the blood trail to the cat in your room -- then turn to the right and stab the toybox.  You land in a dark world that tells the story of the toybox.  First it belonged to Mindy, a little girl who kept her puppets in it.  After her family was dead, it passed to Billy, a science-loving boy who loved bugs.  The toybox developed a fondness for spiders, which it used with Billy's help to kill _that_ family.  Then it passed to your "grandmaw", who bought it for you -- but you never put your toys away, so it couldn't influence you directly (outside of Ending 2).

Over the course of learning the story, you find a yellow key to unlock a yellow door (Mindy) that leads to a room.  In that room are red and blue doors, corresponding to your "grandmaw" and Bully, respectively, and locks of the same colors.  And a huge chain, desceding into darkness.

Each door holds its corresponding key and piece of the story.  Once you find the keys and use them on the locks, the chain pulls up a huge heart.  You stab the heart, and the demon is dead.

... and you have no way to leave the darkness.  But in the end...

... you were a good boy.

The sad part of the idea for [Redacted] is that the number of people who truly experienced it can now ever only decrease.

 The most irretrievable, sad and non-transferrable part is that missing feeling of it being "alive" and "official", of having the liberty to go straight to the channel and see all the vids there and knowing that there would be a new one tomorrow, of living the countdown in real time, feeling its weight and having the comment sections and other social media pages (like the reddit page) to interact with the thriving community who was feeling that weight along with you rather than sadly and nostalgically talking in the past tense about it. Seeing how different people reacted to the incoming demise, from sadness to outright denial was a big part of it too. 

You can look at the memories others have captured but the soul is gone forever, which is a really cool and unique part of the channel. You can probably find that final live stream but the timer won't truly mean anything to you, nor will the end pushing of the delete button since the result of that button being pushed is the only experience you have ever had with the remaining scraps of content left behind and salvaged. Looking back to before the end can and never will be the same as looking forward towards the end and living in the moment.

At some stage, there will only be one person in the entire world who, now a pensioner in their early nineties, will be sitting and reminiscing about two lovable idiots with a deleted Youtube channel. The only one left who once watched them tear phone books, hold viking funerals, sing disclaimer songs, do the dance of Italy, forget the name of a skillet, play nutball, build a dog house, wax each other suggestively, mix pancake batter with a "rubber love sausage", goof around in escape rooms and experience ethical dilemas together. 

I kinda feel bad for whichever one of us that person will be because they will have absolutely no-one who shares these memories with them and truly appreciates the community that once existed there.


(Some cynics will probably bash me a bit for being this dramatic, since "its only a YouTube channel". But you know what, as someone who does English Literature in 17-18 education, if I'm not going to be overly wishy-washy about it then who will, damn it?)

Some advice if you’re ever stuck in a situation where you have to stay in a suspect motel, if you’re traveling, or for any other reason:
1.) Cover mirrors with the towels from the bathroom. If you plan on using the towels, replace them with any other adequately sized linens you don’t intend to use.
2.) Check the insides of ceiling fans, lamps, and telephones for audio bugs and wires.
3.) Before you go to bed, take a shower, or do anything else that would leave you in a compromised position, lever a chair up against the front door. Make sure you get the back of the chair wedged up underneath the door handle.
There’s a lot of weird and evil people out there, and you don’t want to be the one person naive, trusting, or simply unlucky enough to bump into a predator.

agoraphobia is often mistaken as the fear of the outdoors but its actually the crippling anxiety that we will get injured or hurt if we do things outside our very small comfort zones, the fear of inescapable situations, the fear of no escape, no safety. When I brought this up to my own therapist she asked me what I thought the word meant, and once I explained it she agreed that I was infact a sufferer of this haunting condition and further explained that people hear or see the word and think it means the inability to leave the house or go do social things, which is actually introverted or social anxiety, not agoraphobia. As I continue on years after the diagnosis I get hit with another diagnosis of vasovagal syncopy, a condition in which if I am overexerted or overwhelmed I could pass out as my muscles tense too tightly around the vasovagal nerve. I leave the house, I go into stores. I haven't dated or made a friend in years, I haven't been to any social events, only funerals and a few shows, I don't even feel safe at home. I'm a hermit, I'm a shut in. I'm cut off and i'm trying to change. It's not easy. I've been here since day 1 of mark's channel, and during all these years so much has happened, but mark has been a constant in an always changing, always scary world. Never change mark.

Going to bed really was the good ending. AND HERES WHY. 

Because when it comes to depression and other similar disorders, it's about slow progress and taking it a day at a time. 

Just because you are feeling a bit better, doesn't mean you have to push yourself to try and meet the end goal head on, ultimately leading to an anxiety attack or the like. Because that is just going to put you back at square 1. 

It's about accepting small victories and allowing yourself to take breaks. 

Think about it. The player never really sleeps. In the end, the good ending was being ok with letting themself sleep and take a break comfortably, because he worked hard and did a good job. The character did it. They started. 

They made that comfy spot after working hard and facing their demons. The character doesn't have to clean up the whole house in order to have had a productive day. 

For those who are DEEP in depression, often a starting point in getting better is just learning how to be kind to themselves. 

Got out of bed? Brushed your hair? Had a glass of water? 
This is cause to celebrate.

Little victories.

If this person were working with a therapist on what the goal of therapy was, going outside might have been the big overall goal. 

The real meat would have been
-getting out of bed at least 3 times a week. 
-take a bath/ clean up at least once a week
-have at least one good meal everyday. 

You start out with the big stuff. 
You work on it bit by bit. 

Small victories build up to bigger ones.

Two things I love about this game: The comments are full of people sharing their own experiences. Hell, even Mark was talking from experience. The game itself also described it really well. I agree with the others in the comments, that the secret ending is the true ending, the accomplishment of taking care of yourself for the day. 
I do want to say one other thing, though. I also have depression, and the only reason I haven't fallen into those pits for long is because of the "Fuck You" energy that Mark was showing throughout the game. I tell people that everything I do, I've done in spite. They think I'm joking, but I'm not. I persist in spite of what others have told me, and in spite of what my own mind tells me regularly. I've been told it's not a healthy mindset. But depression is numb, it's not sad, at least not for me. It's numb and cold. And numbness leads to inactivity. I channel that numbness into anger, anger is hot and gets me moving. It's not healthy, but it works.

A lot of people are talking about the depressive side of it, but sometimes agoraphobia is closer to severe anxiety. It's hard to keep everything clean and functioning when you're comfortable in chaos, and breaking that pattern really hurts. When "outside" is the monster, you condense your entire life to "inside," regardless of whether or not you actually have the space to do it.

- if you stay in an area for too long, they send more specials to try to get you to move.
- the order of your cards matters (if you’re going to play through a long run) so when you make a deck, put them in the order you want to pick them.
- the ogre tunnels at half health. So you just have to get it to half health in the start and then you’re good to keep moving on.
- and yeah, my friends and I found the jumps between difficulties so insane. The jump from recruit to veteran is insane because it’s like a triple whammy - the ridden to more damage AND you can do team damage AND there and more ridden/specials

So sad to think that Mark may never want to finish this game, but I understand. It's just not the same game anymore. The difference in the handling of gameplay, pacing, story and tone between what was only supposed to be this small slice of the game ahead compared to the game we ultimately got is both frustrating and surreal.

The potential and promise of this first chapter, of what it could be, was so high. A tight, focused, simple yet intriguing and disturbing experience. The succeeding chapters do have a bevy of other smaller improvements like QoL adjustments and consistently great character animation and voice work but nothing that really built upon that core experience that drew people in initially in a satisfying, let alone cohesive, manner.

Maybe we were all giving it too much credit for only being just a demo but... I don't think so. There was something here that was lost. I'm happy Mark stuck it out for as long he could though.

A Walk Home Endings

Ending One: The player makes up with their boyfriend, Jonas. The ending can be achieved by walking straight home without taking any pictures and without looking at the man following you. This includes staying away from places like the cave or shack that can be found in the forest. Once the player reaches their house, they should get a text message from Jonas, thanking you for the visit. Upon receiving the text, head out onto the balcony to see Jonas waving at you from below, and complete the first ending. (Good Ending)

Ending Two: In this ending, the player returns home to be confronted by the man that has been following you. Presumably, one of you die in this scenario, although the game ends before we are shown anything. To get this ending, you must find all of the instances where the killer appears. Along with this, you should also take pictures of blood stains, garbage cans, dead animals, sometimes graffiti or posters, and the man. This includes the cave and shack found in the forest. Upon returning home, you should be locked in and placed into the stand-off with the man.
(Bad Ending)

Ending Three: To achieve the final ending, you must discover every interactable item in the game. This ending is often spotty with its triggering, and there's slight debate online about the exact steps to trigger it. Generally, it is accepted that you must approach the car to set off the alarm, trigger the jump scare in the shack, photograph the animals, and tip over the scooter by the vista. Once you've completed everything, head to the front of your house and hope that you trigger the "behind you" voice line. Once you hear it, turn around and face the street to see a man get ran over. Head inside your house and achieve ending three. The ending's significance is often debated, although most people think you are caught by the police. (Secret Ending)

Overall, the general consensus is that the player is responsible for the missing animals. The man following you home is actually your boyfriend, Jonas, as he suspects you to be involved with the missing animals; hence the posters found inside his house. This is also implied with the photographs reading "He Knows" once triggering the jump scare in the shack. This ending has holes though, and some people point out the man getting ran over in ending three. As far as I could tell, we don't see any dead people throughout the game, only animals. The man in ending three could be referencing ending two, where you presumably kill Jonas for finding out your secret. However, if the man following you home IS Jonas, then that would mean that HE was the person driving the car we see hitting the man in ending three. We know this because the same car that hits the man in the road can be found in the parking lot shortly before you return home. Coincidentally, the man following you is standing next to it before it drives off frantically, eventually returning to kill the man in the street. 

I'm glad Mark got around to playing this game, as it honestly goes a lot deeper than I initially expected. There's still a lot of things that I'm curious about, such as what the true ending really suggests or some of the odd graffiti sprayed on the wall that might imply something deeper. Also, I did notice the 'thunder' that you can hear in Mark's gameplay when he returns to the house. As far as I can tell, this sound effect hasn't played very often or maybe even at all. (Watching again I realize this could be thunder being picked up from Mark's microphone, and might not actually be in the game.) I may be thinking too deep, but I am curious if there is still something hidden within the game that no-one has found yet, even though we've discovered all of the endings. I'd love to see Mark revisit this game to achieve all the endings and maybe start to fall down the same rabbit hole I did while researching the topic. Thanks for the read, guys.

*puts on glasses* As a beekeeper, I'd like to drop a bit of fact here. While it is true bees are very important pollinators, honey bees are not endangered or at risk, in fact commercial beekeepers (not small backyard hobbyists) are part of the problem. It is the Native bees that are endangered. Many native bees are also specialized to certain plants. Some have shorter or longer tongues depending on which plants they specialize in, its called the lock and key principal. While domestic bees can pollinate most things, there are many others that need the touch of specific bees. There are almost 4000 native bee species in the US alone, each specific to their own regions, and not all of them live in hives, quite a lot of them live solitary lives! Commercial beekeepers are just more competition to native bees already struggling, recent studies from the UK prove this. But there are ways to help native bees, some as simple as putting up bee houses for the solitary bees to rest and breed. With hope and innovation, perhaps a balance can be met some day for native and domestic bee alike. *takes off glasses*  Great game tho!  p.s. bees jobs are decided by their age, not by the queen and it is illegal to cut down a tree if there are bees living in it. Nice, but several corrections.
Bees collect the nectar, not the pollen. Collecting pollen is more a thing that just happens without the bees intending to do so. The bees are interested in the nectar of the flowers and the flowers are like "Fine, but could I bother you to take some pollen with your while we are at it?". So the queen bee sending the worker bees out to collect pollen is inaccurate.
Second, a bee doesn't die when stinging other insects and animals. It dies when stinging humans. A bee's stinger has hooks on it. The point if to sting another insect and yank their innards out for maximum damage and insta-kill. Therefore, in the insect world, bees are quite deadly. Problem is only that human skin is very flexible and the hooked stinger just gets stuck there. And when the bee instinctively tries to yank our innards out, it accidentally ripps off its own innards because our skin is less likely to tear then their abdomen.
Third, yes indeed. Bees use dance moves to communicate where they found the most delicious source of nectar.

The thing that happens awakes a sort of ghostly demon monster from another plane and that is why the base is shut down and 'Kill everything' protocol is activated so nothing gets out. 

In regards to the endings. 
With Ending 1, The Car that lands on the broken down car was chucked by the demon monster thing from the car park. So basically - it got out!

My theory on the plot:

As a kid, Peter (MC) went to the park with his real father - Steven - but was lured away by a man dressed as a clown, the clown kidnapped Peter and drove him back to his place, where he locked Peter and two other kids in cages and abused them - the other kids ended up succumbing to their wounds and passing away, but Peter was saved at the expense of serious trauma. At home, Peters sleep was plagued with nightmares of the clown and what happened, which fucked with their mental state as a child and caused them to father a kid that was getting abused - and when feeling threatened caused him to act out and get labeled a maniac.

At some unknown point in Peters early childhood their real parents were murdered and replaced by the "Married Couple" that'd escaped the asylum, Peters then maternal figure abused him because of his trauma induced nightmares and hallucinations - including locking them in the basement and even behind a fake wall where I assume the mannequins were, part of the trauma even caused Peter to go astral and face all their trauma that'd happened to them. To prove that their monsters existed, he set up a noise trap. 3 hours later, his presumed mother went to go down the stairs but triggered the noise trap and fell down the stairs to her death.

Crushed by the thought that he'd just murdered his own mother, Peter hid her body behind the same fake wall he was forced to sleep behind. I'm not too sure about what happened to the presumed father, but Peter was left with heavy trauma. Things looked up at the orphanage, though. Peter eventually stopped having nightmares and even got a psychotherapist who we see in the end. But at the very end it's revealed by the shadow that the doctor - Peter's psychotherapist - was the paternal figure, the one that'd murdered his real father. You can tell this by the Doctor's shadow being a demon.

After watching the behind the scenes of "My house walktrough", here are some interesting facts: 1- Theres no CGI, nana literally redecorated an abandoned house using destroyed old things 2- Nana was apparently scared while recording this, so during the filming, the lights were on. They just added a color filter to the video so it seems like its dark
Edit: Here are some others facts. 3- The house have one long hallways with multiple rooms at the right and the left with a door in the front. The filming process was simple: They decorated the house with broken thing, then they recorded. They redecorated again but this time with blood, they filmed again. Basically, they did that like 4 times and they then edited it to make it look like an endless loop. 4- A lot of people are wondering why is this so scary, simple. The color saturation is WAY too high, wich gives it a really disturbing feeling. It makes it feel like something isn't okay, that something is wrong. They also used a lot of door to give that stressful feeling, because when opening the doors, it feels like there would be a jumpscare but nothing. You are there, waiting for it but it never comes. Also, the Sutra and the rain in the background also plays a big part on the psychology of the viewer. It gives a feel of emptiness, of dead. 5- Also the fact that he keeps repeating things like "This is the alters and ancestors" make it feel like an unending trip. A literal nightmare.

This house can be a metaphor for abuse. Each ending representing a futile way to "fix" it.

In the kill ending, it represents those who lash out with violence. But that doesn't fix it

In the "good" ending, it represents you fixing the smaller issues, saving your mother and your sister. But even if everything seems OK, that doesn't fix the abuse.

The song ending, you can remind the one who's I abusing you how much you love them and reminisce about when things were better. But even if they apologize and promise to fix it, they usually won't.

The killing father ending. You can try to stay in the situation but remove one of the abusers. But if you don't change anything, it's bound to happen again.

The only answer is to leave. Sometimes you can't save those you love. You have to save yourself. And you may lose a piece of yourself. You may be hurt and always have a piece of yourself missing, but it's the only answer

Hey Mark, as someone who has played through the entire game, I have a few tips to make things easier for you.
1. You don’t need to target the insanity thing first in line, so you should instead try to knock off a few singles in order to create sequences of max three that you can then get rid of in one take.
2. Since you get paid more for treating insane patients, I would recommend reading the descriptions of the available patients in order to find the one that seems the most insane.
3. You should absolutely develop all the insanity machines instead of using the default one, it’ll make things much easier for you late game (the more you progress, the more insanity patients have). 
4. If you accidentally delete a patient’s personality (which I’ve done countless times), you don’t need to alt F4, instead you can just go to the menu and rewind to any previous day, which is also useful for achieving different endings based on single decisions.
5. Pay attention to your actions and how it might affect the story. Much like in Papers Please, you either choose to help the resistance group, or work strictly for the government, so make sure not to ignore Moonrise or help the Structure if you’re trying to get the Moonrise ending (the opposite goes for trying to get the Structure ending)

Pro tips:

1. Scrying mirror reveals your location to Jimmy
2. Hiding in the bathroom is a lot less safe than being in the closet
3. Don’t save outside of a room, especially if you aren’t going back to it when you get knocked out. Save after leaving a dangerous situation (using scrying mirror) so you can try again.
4. Lock Jimmy in rooms. Other comments probably show how to do this better, but if you call for Jimmy and leave and you have the key to the room, you can lock it and have some time before he escapes
5. Use the scrying mirror only when you need to or when you are safe. Lower floors, by elevators, etc.
6. Ghost locations are usually signaled by the flickering lights. Follow them to get to the scene, no need to run from them.
7. Jimmy cannot get you if you are in the elevator. If you see him by the elevator, get to it quickly instead of running.
8. Tutorial, Tutorial, TUTORIAL! Trust me, it’s so worth it. Makes the game take less time to complete and gives you lots of good tips.

Hey Mark! Here are some tips to help avoid/hide from Jimmy.
~
He can sometimes camp the exits, so you need to call him to the room you're in and wait until he starts to unlock the door, then hide.

Bathroom: in dark rooms, he'll always figure out you're there. It's a 100% death rate sadly. In normal rooms, I'm pretty sure it's 50/50. I think you have to hide as SOON as he appears through the spy glass.

Closet: Personally I think this is the best hiding spot, I'm pretty sure it has a much lower chance of being caught than the bathroom. Although, with the closet, he can sometimes hide in the bathroom. You need to listen for an audio cue outside before exiting the closet, because if he's not in the bathroom he can be right outside the door.

Locking Jimmy in a room: make sure you have the key to that room. That's important. Call Jimmy/get chased by Jimmy and wait until the very last second of him unlocking the door, then hide in the closet. Wait until you hear a door close and run outside of the room, then lock the door from the outside. He'll be stuck for roughly a minute.

Safe floors: Ground floor, Lower ground floor, and the stairs are all safe spots Jimmy can't go to.

Voice cues are better to gauge where he's at.
~
Hope this helps!

FEW TIPS

if the menu icon on the right bottom corner is red, then you are in danger, most likely Jimmy is in the room, knows where you are or watching you.

the basement, ground floor and stairs are safe zones so you can explore all you want and not get caught by Jimmy. 

the higher the floor the more difficult it is, Jimmy respawns faster the higher you go, 3rd floor being the fastest.

if you have a deadlock key for a room, you can lock Jimmy in there by luring (call out to him) him so he’ll come into the room, when he’s unlocking the door, you need to stand in the middle of the room with you back facing the door, wait and listen closely till he almost swings the door open then hide in the closet so he can see where you’re hiding, he will most likely hide in the bathroom and you just gotta sprint to the door and lock it behind you. 

it’s best if you just look ahead and don’t look behind, one of the best way to play this is just to speedrun it haha

if you’re on your way to the elevator and you see Jimmy on the other end of the hallway across the elevator, just continue and quickly press the elevator, no matter how long the elevator takes to arrive on you floor, Jimmy won’t whack you. Once its open, quickly enter and press the floor and DONT look to the elevator door before pressing the floors bc he WILL get you if you do. Just quickly press the floor and you’re safe

If anyone sees this: Tips for finding unconscious person: 
 Check if the person is still alive:
-first speak, then touch (for example shoulder), then look if the person is still breathing 
when checking for breath, overstretch the neck by tilting the head back, place your ear near the mouth and nose, look towards the chest: chest movement and breath=alive, only one of the two check again or check for pulse.
Breathing:
-> Yes, put patient in recovery position, check vitals reguarly , call ambulance
-> No, begin CPR, order someone to call ambulance:
1. lay the person flat on the back on the ground, avoid soft surfaces
2. Begin CPR by pushing on the chest where the heart is with force. Its not unsusual to break a or multible ribs. 30 pushes, at a speed of about 100 to 120 per minute (help: the beat of the song "staying alive" is perfect) Place the palm of your hand on the chest, place the other hand on top, push at least 2inches (~5cm) in
3. Take a good breath and blow the air into the persons mouth or nose (you can also use something like an oxygen mask, if you have one at hand, to reduce risk of infection), while again overstretching their head, clearing their airways that way, and shutting off the other point of exit (pinch close the nose when breathing through mouth, vise versa) (2x)
then: repeat steps 2 and 3 until ambulance arrives, dont be afraid to ask someone if they can relieve you if you get tired out or feel dizzy
Please like so that more people can save lives

Small hint collection:
-During a hunt, the crucifix does nothing.
Smudge sticks on the other hand, will keep the ghost away from you during a hunt. For that to work, they need to be lit and held in your hand, not thrown.
Then the ghost will stop following you for a little bit. If you break line of sight while the ghost is "confused", the ghost might either wander off or look for another target.
However, if the ghost is a Banshee and you're the selected target, it will resume hunting you until you leave the house or die.
-Audio does not give away your location, line of sight is everything.
-Spirit box only works when the lights in the ghost's room are off.
-The only ghost that can outrun you (as long as you're in sight) is the Revenant. 
Of course, all the other ghosts can sill catch you, if you don't take direct routes or get caught on objects.
-Line of sight will not be broken by doors when the ghost is a Wraith. The Wraith also produces the least amount of stepping noises.
-Poltergeist is the only ghost that leaves fingerprints and ghost orbs. Meaning if both of these appear, it's guaranteed to be a Poltergeist without any further evidence required. 
-If a ghost switches lights on rather than just off, it hints at being either a Poltergeist or Jinn.
-The Mare mostly just turns lights and the fuse box off, but not back on again.
-When your / your teams sanity is high and hunts happen more often than usual, the ghost type is Demon.

This information is unrelated to what Mark did or didn't do, just generally good to know.

I know its been years at this point, but after rewatching for the sake of it, I decided to do some research on that Russian MRE. That weird stuff was called kasha, a buckwheat porridge with beef. And Mark in fact did cook it correctly, but didn't cut it up first to prevent it from burning at the bottom. And yes, he did in fact dump an entire packet of sugar into water. My best guess for the circular tins is that one was a vegetable caviar and the other was a salmon pâté. Most of the stuff there was meant to be used to spread onto the crackers, as it seems that they can come in two flavors, one being sweet and the other being savory. The apple stuff was an apple preserve. There's also many, and I mean many, different powders. There's the coffee packet that I saw, the tea bags, sugar packets, salt, pepper, and from what I've researched, there's apparently water purification tablets inside. It seems that each Russian MRE comes in a box with a number inside to designate the menu items inside, so a MRE with a menu labelled 1 will have slightly different stuff inside than a 3 or 5. They also tend to have napkins inside.

Here's how I think the game engine achieves the forced perspective mechanic in this game.

When you pick up an object, the game measures the distance between the first person camera and the next collision surface like a wall or floor. It also notes that objects scale value. When you let go of the object, the game does the same thing, except this time if the distance from the camera to the next collision surface has increased, the objects scale value is increased or vice versa. Just before the game applies physics to the object, it moves the object as far away from the camera as possible until it hits a collision surface, applies the scale value, and then applies physics.

tips

Smiley ( glowing runes ). There's a note explaining that he won't attack if you stand still. This obviously isn't the case if you're stood in front of his path when walking.

The Witch ( Screamy, chases you a lot ). You can hear her coming by her music. You need to run away and break line of sight.

Clubfoot ( some people call him tree man ). There is a note saying to not look at him. You can hear his heavy breathing when he is near. Don't look at him directly or he will attack. You do have a brief grace window if he triggers.

Wickerman ( Big tree with a deer skull ). Stay away from him, you can hear his creaks as he moves around. He can outrun you but if you're fast enough to make it to a fire or indoors, he will de-aggro you.

For those of you who want to know when every monster attacks:
|
|
v

Spider:
When too much noise is made, a large spider-like creature will appear from the Earth. It will try to either kill one of you or take one you to its nest (underground across the map) the Spider takes you to its nest the first time it captures you. The second time it attacks you, you will be killed instead of taken to its nest.

Skinny:
The Skinny is the most common monster/enemy you will find around the map. You will know when they are near when you hear some sort of gargling noise. It makes it's noise for maybe around 3-4 seconds. The Skinnies are blind and are only attracted to noise or if you get in a certain radius of them. When the Skinny attacks, it will rush into your face. The Skinny can only be stunned by a flare or flare gun. When you shoot a flare gun at it, it will stun it for maybe around 10 seconds. Using a flare is best used when the Skinny rushes at you.

Tall boy:
The Tall boy stands still and looks like a tree. Upon closer inspection, they look like a skinny but a bit fatter and tall as a tree. The Tall boys seem to be like sentries and when you walk near them. the tall boy will not kill you but once it sees you it will make noise to attract other monsters.

I play this game a lot: Here are some tips:

You can hide in any room besides the ghosts room, and multiple people can be in 1 room at a time to hide
To smudge an area, light it inside the room and throw it on the floor. This also can stop the ghost from having any activity if it is a spirit.
If you throw the crucifix on the floor in front of the ghost, and it walks within a foot of it, it will stop from attacking if you put it down before the hunt.
Saying its name and a question within the same sentence doesn't work. Say only a sentence or only its name at once.
Spirit box responds to questions without its name. 
Parabolic mic doesn't work well on the high school or asylum (big maps)
The lower your sanity, the more the ghost hunts.
Carrying a candle can keep your sanity up longer.

14:56 i don't know if he or anyone else wants potential answers for this but it could be a lot of things. my theory is that when you're doing it for the first time, you're following the momentum and instinct and flow of all of the movement before it. when you return, your brain is cluttered with thoughts about how you failed previously and what you might need to do/think you need to do, plus you're already flustered from failing before. this makes it harder to complete the task, even though theoretically it should be easier because you have more knowledge and experience when you return than when you attempted it for the first time. "beginner's luck" is a real thing, in that your first attempt at something might go great if you manage to just do what feels right and not overthink it, but if you've already failed once, you're a lot more likely to overthink your next attempt

Some bits of knowledge people should have for this game
Saying any swears, "Bloody Mary", "Run", and "I'm leaving" make the ghost angry
Saying the ghost's name can and will anger a ghost more than anything else. Ghost's name can even get a shade mad, I believe.
Saying "Give us a sign!" will make the ghost do stuff like making water dirty, moving objects, and flickering lights
Saying "Show us a sign!" will make the ghost get very mad
Saying "Close this door" or "Turn this light off" will make the ghost do that (if they want too)
The only time angering words can be said without triggering the ghost's anger is inside the van BEFORE THE VAN DOOR IS OPENED
Hope these tips help everyone!

Here are a few tips from Jack's video, thought it would be useful here:

ON the radio, if the ghost starts to say "death, kill, attack" that means it is getting ready to/already HUNTING
When the ghost HUNTS it picks a player to chase and attempt to kill.
When the lights and flashlights repeatedly flicker, find a closet and hide in it and do not speak in voice chat, stay silent. That is your best chance of survival.
If you hear heartbeats, -DO THE PREVIOUS STEP FASTER-, this means YOU are a target, if the ghost touches you, you will die
Depending on the ghost, more then one or even everyone's heart will beat, meaning the ghost only wants the first one it catches.
First step I usually take, is keep any closet you come across in mind for hiding, then set up equipment.

some ghosts kill faster, some not at all.
the DEMON and MARE are two of the fastest killers, as they hunt very frequently. however the MARE only hunts fast if the PLAYERS are in the dark. [Nightmare anyone?]
the SPIRIT and SHADE are some of the slowest, the spirit is the most common ghost, and the shade is very shy.
ONI also hunts rather fast, but not as fast as the DEMON

no matter the ghost, saying its name will anger it, the more you say it, the more likely it will spook you, or even attack. Even SHADES get pissed at this!
You do not have to say the ghosts name in a question, simply asking "are you here" or "are you near" are fine, saying its name only provokes it so it can speak, which is normally not needed if you found the room it is mainly haunting.

A fair bit of rambling hypothesis for a few things:
The ending, with the apartment being a dream, poses the question. Would you rather live peacefully in a fake world, or break free and fight your way forward in the truth. On one hand, you could fade, becoming one with the woods. On the other, you could push forward, to freedom or otherwise. 

The ending lines, talking about the people just burning up as they were stuck or refused to run, represent people stuck in their ways and refusing to progress. The only people not caught in the fire or known to be dead are Piotreck, who innovated and dreamed of escape, eventually reaching the stars, if only briefly. The other is the Wolf, who's ruthlessness and cunning would serve him well to escape, as he had no attachments to his land.

There's so many ways to look at this game. Is this an SCP adjacent thing, in real life, that overtook a large area of land? Something more supernatural? A representation of a disease? Or just the ramblings of a madman?

"I should have thought of the consequences of putting a mushroom that is used to modify my character, into the hands of a child."
This line hits really hard. Not just because of what happened in the game, but just in general. Imagine how many methods in games are used to boost your character like this, that would be super horrible in reality. Obviously as a character you can survive because it's meant for you, but I'd love to see a game that explores non player characters messing with game mechanics that would be horrible for them.

The theory I'm working with:
This game so far has been purposefully unfair in certain aspects (like feeding the musician the wrong thing), and the entire story is dark, gloomy and unforgiving. I think the developers weaved that idea into the gameplay. To give you the sense of no matter what you do, no matter what your intentions are, the worst happens. And honestly, I think that's the theme of the game. The game isn't fair because well, life isn't fair. You may have the best intentions while doing something, but that doesn't mean that it won't backfire, and create something horrible instead. I think that's the message of the game, and I'm loving it so far!

Regarding 10:08: Mark, if you read this, and haven’t figured it out by yourself, the reason your trap (and then your shotgun) couldn’t kill the Chomper wasn’t because it didn’t do a lot of damage. It was because of the black fog that the Chomper was bathed in. The fog is alive, and it makes whatever it clings to invincible. However, it dies and melts away in the light. So you have to trick foggy enemies into going into light areas to melt their fog armor and make them killable.

The fog also likes to manifest on chests and other interactable objects, preventing you from opening them. In order to access certain areas and solve puzzles, you have to startle the giant floor-eyeballs that you hate so much. When you scare certain eyeballs, they close their lid and shine a bioluminescent light nearby, which burns away the fog and makes the item usable.

As someone who played this game years ago, I only have this to say: Darkwood is a terrible experience that I highly suggest.

The thing is, even though the trader lied and kept the key from you, he was technically in the right in preventing you from continuing
Most people boil it down to him lying to keep the player in Chapter 1 so he won’t leave him behind to be lonely and while that reason is partially true, there is a more selfless part to it
The Trader says on multiple occasions that escape is impossible and that you’re only heading deeper into the forest’s jaws, saying “The forest wants to devour you. You're heading straight into its jaws” in the old woods hide out.
The entire time the player wasn’t escaping from the forest but the opposite, going inwards till he finds the center
If that really was the way out, wouldn’t the Trader at least attempt to head to the Swamp as he already had the key on his person
The trader knows that heading deeper into the woods is practically a death trap, which is why he spends his time in the Chapter one area, the safest and (technically) outermost part of the woods
If he were to give you the key, he would be leading you to your own demise at the hands of the unforgiving forest
I know this doesn’t take away from the selfish primary reason that he kept the key from you so that you wouldn’t leave him alone but nobody does stuff for purely selfish or selfless reasons. His decisions likely stemmed from both selfish (loneliness) and selfless (preventing you from marching to your death) reasons
The Trader is still the most sympathetic character of the bunch

Hey Mark. That red light that appeared in your hideout is called "Glare." You can look at it as long as you are outside of the red aura. If you are, however, in the red aura, don't look at the white core. That's what causes the PAIN debuff. 

Also, when you are about to face off with a Banshee, you have a 50/50 chance of being able to face the wall and it'll just go away. 

A third thing. When you see Mushrooms, be wary. They may be mushroom men. If they are, run. And if you don't get away, have bandages on hand. Do not try to melee fight these things. It's a bad idea. Trust me.

Finally, be careful around the Old Woods. Be observant. Respect them. If you don't, who knows what the trees will throw at you. Treat every day like you're about to face every enemy at once. Only then will you hope to survive.
